title: Ordering now tells the truth and never dead-ends.
summary: The Jobs to order list now shows each job's real system and square footage (they used to read blank next to a working material total). Touch-up callbacks no longer clutter the list. When the calculator cannot make lines, the row now says the real reason, for example that Custom System has no material recipe, and every such job has an Add lines by hand button so nothing is stuck. Typing a quantity or ticking ordered on a calculated job saves its lines for you automatically. And when nothing is selected, the order sheet now tells you to tick the jobs above, with a Select all button right there.
howto: Open Ordering. Tick the jobs you want to order for, or use Select all shown; the order sheet builds from your selection.
For a job with no recipe (like Custom System), click Add lines by hand on its row and pick the products.
Edit quantities right in the order sheet. On a calculated job the first edit saves the lines automatically.

title: A follow-up queue that tells you who to call first, and what to say.
summary: The new Follow-ups page (under Sales Activity) lists every sent estimate that has gone 3 or more days without a real human touch, ranked by who is most worth calling today. Each row shows how long they have been quiet, whether they have been opening their proposal, and a suggested opener written from your own sales playbook and what actually happened on the visit, with a copy button. Automatic drip messages never count as a touch, so the list reflects real human follow-up. You can also log a touch (a call, a text, or they walked into the shop) from the queue, the customer page, or the estimate page, and that note shows up everywhere.
howto: Open Sales Activity, then Follow-ups. The hottest follow-up is on top; use the suggested opener or the ready-to-send text.
After you reach out, click Log a touch so the clock resets and the row leaves the queue.
If a customer names a date, use Snooze. Tune thresholds and the morning Slack digest in Settings, then Follow-ups.

title: Every lead now gets a score, and it refreshes nightly.
summary: The Hot, Warm, Cold badge on the Pipeline is now real for every lead. A lead gets its AI score the moment it arrives, whether it came from the website form, a Routemize booking, or was typed in by hand. Each morning the open pipeline re-scores automatically, so the badge reflects what has happened since (an estimate sent, a call logged), not just how the lead looked the day it came in. Hover a badge to see when it was last scored. A lead with no score yet shows Not scored yet instead of nothing.
howto: On the Pipeline, set Sort to AI score: hot first to work the hottest leads first. Leads without a score group at the end until their first nightly run.
Hover any Hot, Warm, or Cold badge to see the score reason and when it was scored.
Tune it in Settings, then Drips, under Lead scoring: turn the nightly re-score on or off and cap how many leads score per night.

title: See your whole Google calendar in TopCoat.
summary: Each salesperson can now pick which of their Google calendars sync into TopCoat, not just the dedicated TopCoat calendar. Imported events show on the Appointments calendar with a small G badge, visible to all staff. Events you own move both ways (drag them in TopCoat and Google follows); events you cannot edit in Google (subscriptions, other people's invites) show as read only with the reason. Imported events are time blocks only: they never text a customer, never send a reminder, and never move a lead.
howto: Go to Settings, then Appointments. Under Google Calendar sync, click Refresh list next to a connected salesperson to load their calendars.
Tick the calendars to sync. Events land on the Appointments calendar within about 15 minutes.
On the Appointments calendar, use the Hide Google-imported checkbox when you only want to see real bookings.

title: Rescheduling in Routemize now moves the appointment in TopCoat.
summary: Before this fix, editing or rescheduling an appointment in Routemize left the old time on the TopCoat calendar and on Google. Updates now apply everything Routemize sends (new time, address, assigned rep, notes), cancellations made inside a Routemize edit are recognized, and any webhook event that lands without being applied raises an alert instead of staying silent.
howto: Nothing to set up. Reschedule in Routemize as usual; the TopCoat calendar and the Google event follow automatically.
A reschedule shows up in the notification bell and on the lead's timeline, with the old and new times.
If an event ever fails to apply, it appears on the Ops Queue under Routemize events not applied, and a bell notification points you there.

title: New Settings page: Radar, the early warning system's dials and its open findings.
summary: Business Radar watches the phone log, the CRM, and email for problems (an unreturned call, a complaint, money aging on a finished job, a big estimate going cold) and records findings so nothing gets raised twice. The new Settings, Radar page holds every threshold it fires on and shows the findings that are still open, with their age.
howto: Open Settings and pick Radar in the left rail.
The switch turns radar on or off. Missed call grace sets how long an unreturned call can sit before it fires.
Open Advanced for the other thresholds: AR aging, cold estimates, callback SLA, escalation and mute windows.

title: The Generate Scope button is gone. Picking a system writes the scope now.
summary: When you pick a system on an estimate line, that system's scope template drops straight into the line description, ready to edit. No more Generate button and no more AI rewrite: what you see on the line is exactly what the customer reads. Your own typed text is never replaced without asking first.
howto: In the estimator, add a line and pick a system. The template appears in the description immediately.
Edit the text freely. If you change the system later, it asks before replacing anything you wrote.
Templates are edited in Catalog, System types, Edit. Each system has a standard and an optional MVB version.

title: Templates can ask for job details with fill-in fields
summary: A scope template can carry named placeholders like {{install_date}} or {{stem_walls}}. When the template lands on a line, a short form appears under the description with one box per placeholder. Filling a box drops the answer straight into the text. An estimate cannot be sent while any placeholder is unfilled.
howto: Write a placeholder in a template as two curly braces around a lowercase name, like {{install_date}}. A name ending in _date gets a date picker.
On the line editor, fill each box; the answer replaces the placeholder in the text.
The send button stays blocked until every placeholder, BLANK, and ___ is filled in.

title: Metrics now tracks how often you close in the home
summary: An accepted estimate counts as sold on site when the customer accepted during your on-site visit (up to 2 hours after the appointment ends, adjustable). Metrics shows the rate, the raw count, and each salesperson's in-home numbers. Every accepted estimate shows what the rule decided and lets you correct it by hand.
howto: Open Metrics. The Sold on site card sits with the sales cards; click it for the estimates behind the number.
On an accepted estimate, the Sold on site box under the signature shows why it counted or not. Tick or untick to correct it.
Tune the grace window and appointment types in Settings, Estimates, Sold on site tracking.

title: Your address and ROC number at the top of every estimate
summary: Customer estimates now show your showroom address, phone, license number, and website right under the logo, visible without scrolling. The footer keeps them too for printed pages. Settings, Brand also gained a PEC / FTP switcher so both brands' details can be edited.
howto: Open any customer estimate link. The letterhead sits under the logo at the top.
To change the details, open Settings, Brand, pick the brand, edit, and save.
Finishing Touch has no ROC on file yet. Switch to FTP and enter it, and its estimates pick it up.

title: Color charts on customer estimates
summary: Each line's system now shows its color chart on the customer's estimate, built straight from your product catalog. A flake job shows the flake colors, a metallic job the metallic pigments, and the customer's chosen color is marked so they see it in context of the whole range.
howto: Send or preview any estimate with a flake, metallic, or quartz line. The charts appear below the price.
The chosen color carries a Your selection badge.
Tune or turn this off under Settings, Estimates, Color charts on customer estimates. Charts only appear for products with images in the catalog.

title: Your warranty on every estimate, frozen at send
summary: Write your warranty once under Settings, Presentation, and it appears on every customer estimate right after the terms. The wording freezes when an estimate is sent, so a customer always sees the exact warranty their document went out with, even if you edit it later.
howto: Open Settings, Presentation and add a section with the kind Our warranty.
Send an estimate. The warranty shows after the terms and is frozen for that customer.
Turn it on or off under Settings, Estimates, Warranty on customer estimates.

title: A real calendar for the Job Schedule on your phone
summary: On a phone, the 3-week Job Schedule now shows one week at a time as a real calendar grid. Job bars span their days in crew colors, just like on the computer. Swipe left or right to change weeks, and the week you were on is remembered if the page reloads.
howto: Open Job Schedule on your phone in 3 weeks mode. You will see this week as a seven-day grid.
Swipe the calendar left or right (or tap the arrows above it) to move between weeks.
Tap any day's header to open that day's full run sheet under the grid. Tap a job bar for its details.

title: Notifications panel now fits on your phone
summary: The notification bell's panel used to open partly off the screen on phones. It now always fits the screen, scrolls inside itself when the list is long, and closes when you tap anywhere outside it.
howto: Tap the bell in the top bar. The panel opens fully on screen at any phone size.
Scroll inside the panel if you have a long list of notifications.
Tap outside the panel (or press Escape on a keyboard) to close it.

title: The bell rings when a payment comes in
summary: You now get a notification for every payment: a customer paying by card, a bank (ACH) payment settling, a bank payment failing, and payments the office records by hand. A failed bank payment rings loud, because money that looked collected has vanished. Tapping a payment notification opens that job's invoice.
howto: Watch the bell in the top bar. New payments show the customer, amount, and method.
Tap a payment notification to open that job's invoice screen.
Tune it under Settings, Invoicing, Payment bell notifications. You can set a minimum amount so tiny test charges stay quiet.

title: CompanyCam photos on estimates and proposals
summary: Estimates now show the job's CompanyCam photos while you price, matched automatically by customer name. Every photo starts ticked; ticked photos appear on the customer's proposal in a Photos from your site visit section, and the set freezes when you send. New photos taken before the send are included automatically.
howto: Open an estimate. The CompanyCam photos card links the matching project by itself, or search and pick one.
Untick any photo the customer should not see. The count line shows how many will go out.
Send the estimate as usual. The proposal carries the ticked photos, frozen at that moment.
Tune it under Settings, Estimates, CompanyCam photos on estimates.

title: New estimates: options start unticked, payment schedule fills itself in
summary: Two defaults changed for newly started estimates. Optional line items now start unselected on the proposal, so customers add what they want instead of removing what they do not. And the payment schedule now appears automatically with the standard 50 percent deposit, which had stopped happening on estimates started from the dashboard.
howto: Start an estimate as usual. The payment schedule card is already filled in with the default deposit; edit or remove it if the job needs different terms.
Mark a line Optional and it lands in Options to add, unticked. Use the Starts selected checkbox on the line if you want it pre-picked.
The old pre-selected default is one switch away under Settings, Estimates, Optional lines.

title: Cleaner estimate page
summary: The Pricing logic and Pricing intelligence boxes are gone from the estimate page. All the numbers behind them are still calculated and stored; the page just no longer shows those two cards.
howto: Open any estimate. The right column now goes from the job info to sales visit recording, CompanyCam photos, activity, and communications.

title: Print the customer proposal or invoice right from the dashboard
summary: You can now print or save a PDF of the exact proposal or invoice your customer sees, without leaving the dashboard. The estimate page has a new Print / PDF button that works even before the estimate is sent, and the invoice's More actions menu item now prints the customer's invoice page.
howto: Open an estimate and click Print / PDF in the toolbar. The customer proposal opens with the print window ready.
On an invoice, open More actions and choose Print / Save as PDF.
In the print window, pick your printer to print, or choose Save as PDF to keep a file.

title: Creating a job for a repeat customer now asks: same job, or a new one?
summary: When you add a job for a customer who already has an open job on the other side of the system, a chooser appears before saving. Pick Link to connect the two records so ordering, costing, and the budget all read one job card, or pick Separate new job to keep them fully independent. Linked jobs stay correctly matched even when a customer has two jobs at the same name and address.
howto: Add a job from the Job Schedule (+ Add Job) or the Jobs page (New Job) as usual.
If that customer already has an open job on the other side, the chooser lists each one. Pick Link to existing if it is the same job.
Pick Separate new job if it really is a second job. It will never be mixed up with the other one, even at the same address.

title: See every text, call, and email right on the estimate
summary: Each estimate now has a Communications card showing the full text and call history with that customer plus every email sent to them, with Call and Text buttons. The send window also shows the sign-here button and link that ride under your message, so you can see exactly what the customer will get.
howto: Open any estimate and scroll to the Communications card in the right column.
Use the Text button to jump into that customer's message thread; texts sent there always carry the live estimate link.
Click an email row to see its full content and open tracking.

title: Job pages now show the install schedule for every kind of job
summary: A job created in TopCoat or added by hand on the calendar now shows its scheduled install dates on the job page, matching the Job Schedule. Before, only jobs that came in through DripJobs could see their own schedule there.
howto: Open any job from the Jobs page.
The header shows the scheduled install date pulled straight from the Job Schedule calendar.
If a job still reads Unscheduled, it has no calendar entry yet (or the calendar entry's name and address do not match the job).

title: Custom estimate jobs now show their line items and price
summary: Jobs created from a signed custom estimate (and any estimate with add-on lines) now carry every sold line onto the job page. Before this fix, a custom estimate's job showed an empty line items table and a zero price.
howto: Open the job from the Jobs page.
The Line Items table now shows each sold line with its price and scope.
The one affected job (EST-102098) was repaired automatically, nothing to redo.

title: TopCoat now checks its own machinery every morning
summary: A daily heartbeat verifies every scheduled job ran, webhooks and messages are not failing, the Google review link works, Stripe payments are not stuck, and customer pages load. Problems show up in the Ops Queue and one Slack line; silence means everything is green.
howto: Open Settings, then System health, to see the latest run and every job's last heartbeat.
Use Run now to check everything on demand.
Red findings also appear under System health in the Ops Queue until they clear.

title: Appointments link customers, with real search and automatic titles
summary: The appointment form now links a customer instead of a lead. Type a few letters of a name, phone, or address to find them, or create a new customer right in the form. Titles fill in automatically, like On-site estimate for Tom Bechtel. The Customers page also gained All, Customers, and Prospects filters.
howto: Open Appointments and click a time slot, then start typing in the Customer box to search.
Pick a match or use New customer to add one without leaving the form.
The title writes itself from the customer and appointment type; blocks with no customer keep a free text title.

title: Google Calendar sync repaired, with honest reconnect prompts
summary: Appointments booked through Routemize now push to your TopCoat Google calendar just like in-app bookings. If Google ever stops accepting a saved connection, Settings shows a Reconnect button and you get one bell notification instead of a silently frozen calendar.
howto: Open Settings, then Appointments, and look at the Google Calendar sync card.
If your row says Sync stopped, click Reconnect and sign in with the same Google account.
New appointments from any source then appear in your TopCoat calendar within seconds.

title: Slack cheers when an estimate is accepted
summary: The #epoxysales message for an accepted estimate is now a proper celebration: the customer, estimate number, total, and the salesperson who sold it, with a shout-out. You can turn just the accept post on or off without touching the view alerts.
howto: Nothing to do; accepted estimates post to #epoxysales automatically.
To turn it off, open Settings > Estimates and untick the celebration box inside the Slack alert card.

title: The estimator saves your work automatically
summary: Estimates now save themselves a couple of seconds after every change, and again the moment you switch apps or close the tab. The bar at the bottom shows the live status: Saving, All changes saved with the time, or Offline, saved on this device. The Save button is still there for an instant save. A brand new estimate first saves once it has a customer and at least one priced line, so empty drafts no longer appear in the list.
howto: Just build the estimate; watch the bottom bar say All changes saved.
Offline in a driveway, the bar says saved on this device and it syncs when you get signal.
If the bar says Save failed or needs your OK, press Save.

title: A cleaner estimator screen
summary: The Comparable jobs and AI price read boxes are gone from the estimator. The analysis still runs in the background on every new estimate, and the result shows on the estimate page in the office. Pricing in the estimator itself is unchanged.
howto: Build estimates as usual; the screen just has less to scroll past.
To see the comps and the AI read for an estimate, open its estimate page from the Estimates list.
Settings > Estimates > Pricing intelligence still controls the background analysis.

title: Confetti when an estimate is accepted
summary: When a customer signs their estimate, every open dashboard fires a confetti burst and a toast with the customer, estimate number, and total. If it happened while nobody was looking, the next person to open the dashboard gets the celebration once. Each browser celebrates each acceptance one time only.
howto: Keep the dashboard open and the celebration pops within about a minute of an acceptance.
Turn it on or off in Settings > Estimates under Accept celebration on the dashboard.
Devices set to reduced motion skip the animation and still show the toast.

title: Offboard a login without losing any history
summary: Settings > People can now revoke a person's login: they are signed out everywhere within a minute, cannot sign back in, and every record they touched keeps their name. Their sales and crew roles are untouched. You can reassign their open items to someone else during the revoke, and a Restore login button undoes it later with the same email, password, and permissions.
howto: Open Settings > People and click the person, then Revoke login in their Login section.
Pick who receives their open items, or choose Do not reassign, and confirm.
To bring them back later, open the same card and click Restore login.

title: The estimator Save button now stays on screen on your phone
summary: On phones, the Save button rides in a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen, so it is visible at every scroll position, with the reason it is disabled named right beside it. The estimator also checks for a newer version when it opens: a fresh screen updates itself, and if you are mid-estimate it shows a small note asking you to reload after saving instead of interrupting you.
howto: Open the estimator on your phone; the Save bar sits at the bottom of the screen the whole time.
If you see a note that a newer version is available, finish and save, then reload the page.

title: One combined page for a signed estimate and its job
summary: Once an estimate becomes a job, opening either record lands on one combined page, the way DripJobs shows a deal. The job page now has Job, Estimate, and Messages and Calls tabs. The Estimate tab shows the estimate number, status, price, line items, scope, and when the customer opened it. The full estimate page (edit, re-send, present) is one click away via Open estimate page.
howto: Open any signed estimate from the Estimates list or pipeline; you land on the combined page.
Use the Job, Estimate, and Messages and Calls tabs under the header.
Need to edit or re-send the estimate? Tap Open estimate page on the Estimate tab.

title: Jump between an estimate, its job, and its invoice
summary: The three records for one sale are now tied together. A signed estimate's page has Open job and View invoice buttons in the toolbar, the job page has a View Estimate button, and the invoice page has an Open estimate button next to Open job card. No more hunting through lists to find the matching record.
howto: Open a signed estimate and use Open job or View invoice in the top toolbar.
From a job card, tap View Estimate to see the estimate it came from.
From an invoice, tap Open estimate.

title: The estimator got tabs and three kinds of notes
summary: The estimate editor is tidier: Estimate type and Salesperson share one card, the comps and AI price panels tuck away until you tap them, and a new Settings and Notes tab strip sits under the columns. Settings holds the payment schedule and shows where the deposit percent comes from. Notes now has three lanes: Crew notes (team only, prints on the work order), Client notes (the customer reads these on their estimate as 'A note from us'), and Company notes (office only, never sent).
howto: Open any estimate and use the Settings and Notes tabs under the main columns.
Type a client note in the Notes tab and preview the estimate; it appears above the line items.
Tap Comparable jobs or AI price read on the right to expand them when you want them.

title: The estimate's investment summary got a clearer look
summary: The Your investment section on the customer estimate now shows the subtotal, a highlighted Deposit to start row, and a bold band with the project total on the left and the balance at completion on the right. All three update live as the customer ticks optional add-ons, and an accepted estimate keeps showing exactly the numbers that were signed.
howto: Nothing to do: every estimate page shows the new summary automatically.
Preview any open estimate and tick an optional line to watch the deposit and balance update.

title: Empty estimates can no longer be sent
summary: An estimate with no priced lines, or one that adds up to zero, can no longer be sent to a customer by any path: email, text, or opening it for signing in Present mode. The send now stops with a clear message telling you to open the estimate in the estimator, add at least one line, and save first. The same check runs on the server too, so even an old open tab cannot slip a blank estimate out.
howto: Nothing to do for normal estimates: anything with at least one priced line sends exactly as before.
If a send is blocked with 'This estimate has no priced lines yet', open the estimate, use Edit to add and price its lines, save, and send again.

title: Sent estimates stay marked Sent, even after edits
summary: A sent estimate no longer slips back to In Draft when someone re-saves it from the estimator. Sending is now the only thing that sets the sent state, the database itself refuses any change that would move an estimate backward, and every list, badge, and pipeline card reads the same truth. If a sent estimate is edited afterward, its page now shows a notice that the customer's link already has the new numbers, with a Re-send button right there.
howto: Nothing to do: estimates you send now stay Sent everywhere, including after edits.
If you edit an estimate after sending it, look for the orange notice at the top of its page and use Re-send so the customer knows to take a fresh look.

title: The invoice page got a cleaner layout with tabs
summary: The invoice screen now leads with the two buttons you actually use (Send invoice and Receive payment) plus a More actions menu for everything else, one info card with the client, invoice number, date invoiced, due date, terms, and salesperson, and three tabs underneath: Invoice (line items, change orders, payments), Settings (payment schedule, deposit, void), and Notes (every email and text sent). Two new abilities: Customer view opens the exact page the customer sees, and Void invoice cancels an invoice cleanly (it leaves every list and total, and its pay link goes dead).
howto: Open any invoice from Invoicing; switch tabs to move between the line items, the payment schedule, and the send history.
Use More actions for the PDF, the public link, card charges, line edits, change orders, and voiding.
Add or fix a due date right on the info card with Add due date or Edit terms.

title: New estimates come with the payment schedule already filled in
summary: Every new estimate now starts with the default payment plan: the deposit (at the system type's percent, or the company default) and the remaining balance due at completion. That means every proposal a customer opens shows the payment schedule without the rep having to build one. You can still change it, add installments, or remove it on any estimate, and once you touch it the estimator stops auto-filling for that estimate. Opening an old estimate never re-adds a schedule that was removed.
howto: Start a new estimate and price it; the Payment schedule card fills itself in and shows on the proposal.
Edit or remove the schedule on the card if a job needs something different.
To go back to the old build-it-yourself behavior, open Settings, go to Invoicing, and turn off 'Start new estimates with the default schedule'.

title: Invoices now state their payment terms at the top
summary: Every invoice now carries payment terms, shown at the top of the customer's invoice page and on the PDF: residential jobs default to Due upon completion, and commercial clients default to Net 30 with the due date counted from the day the invoice first goes out. You can change any single invoice's terms from its Edit terms button, and payment reminders now wait for the due date instead of nudging a Net 30 customer three days after the send. When an invoice has a payment schedule, the schedule still decides what is due and when; the terms line is informational.
howto: Nothing to do for defaults: new jobs pick their terms from the client type automatically (a business name or commercial estimate means commercial).
To change one invoice, open it in Invoicing and use the Edit terms button next to the terms line.
To change the company defaults, open Settings, go to Invoicing, and set the Residential and Commercial dropdowns under Invoice terms.

title: Customers are asked how they want to pay the moment they sign
summary: Right after a customer signs their estimate, the page now shows their invoice amount and asks how they want to pay: card or bank through Stripe, check, cash, Zelle, or financing. Before, the page only sometimes showed a small deposit link, and a customer could sign and walk away without ever being asked. The prompt shows whatever is currently due, whether that is the deposit, a scheduled installment, or the balance. Choosing check, cash, or Zelle notifies the office automatically so you can watch for it. You can turn the prompt off in Settings.
howto: Nothing to do: every estimate signed from now on shows the payment chooser automatically.
The customer can also skip it; the invoice link stays right there and you can still send the invoice yourself as before.
To turn it off, open Settings, go to Invoicing, and flip 'Ask for payment right after signing'.

title: Invoice numbers are now numbers only
summary: Every invoice now shows a clean all-digit number. New jobs automatically get the next number in a series starting at 10001, and the handful of older invoices that displayed a short code with letters were given real numbers. Invoices that already showed a numeric DripJobs number keep it, so nothing a customer has already seen changes.
howto: Nothing to do: numbers are assigned automatically when a job is created.
You can still type your own number on a job if you ever need a specific one.

title: Customer info now sits locked at the top of the estimate
summary: In the estimator, the customer card no longer lives as a box in the left column. Once the customer's info is entered it collapses into a compact bar across the top of the estimate showing the name, type, phone, email, and address. The bar is locked so nothing gets bumped while you work the estimate; tap it any time to reopen the full card and edit.
howto: Start a new estimate and fill in the customer as usual, then tap Done (or pick an existing customer from search) and the card locks into the top bar.
Tap the bar whenever you need to change something; tap Done to lock it again.
Opening an existing estimate shows the bar already locked.

title: Edit the flake color right from the job, and picking it confirms colors
summary: The Colors card on a job's detail page now has a flake color box with the full list of blends to pick from, so you can set or change the color without opening the estimate. It writes to the same place the estimate page does, and saving a color also marks the job's colors confirmed in the same click, since picking the color is the confirmation.
howto: Open the job, find the Colors card on the Details tab, type or pick the flake color, and hit Save color.
Colors flip to confirmed automatically when you save a color; the Unconfirm button still works if plans change.

title: The production calendar comes back to this week after scheduling
summary: After you schedule or reschedule a job, the calendar now returns to the current week. Before, it jumped to the week of the job's earliest scheduled day, which for a rescheduled job was often its original date from weeks back.
howto: Schedule a job as usual; when the modal closes you land on today's week.
Use the arrows or the Today button to move around like always.

title: Estimates made of only custom lines now save, and Save always tells you what is missing
summary: An estimate whose only line was a custom line (a typed price with no square footage) could not be saved: the Save button simply never appeared, on phones and desktops alike. That is fixed. A custom-line-only estimate now prices like any other (the total is the sum of your typed prices, with real GP from the typed cost and hours), and the Save button now shows on every estimate, in every state. When something still blocks saving, the button sits disabled with a short note beside it naming exactly what to fix, like the custom line that needs a price or the area that needs square footage.
howto: Add a custom line, type its price (plus material cost and crew hours if you want GP), fill in the customer, and Save works with no areas at all.
If Save is greyed out, read the note next to it: it names the exact thing blocking the save.
Mixed estimates still work the same: calculator areas price from square footage and custom lines add their typed price on top.

title: The black bar on modals is gone, and email buttons now always look like buttons
summary: Every modal opened from the dashboard had a dark bar across the top; that bar is gone and the close X now sits in a small white circle that stays put while you scroll. Customer emails got a matching fix: the View and sign, View Invoice and Pay, and Review and sign buttons are now added automatically under your message when you send, in the brand accent color, centered. Before this, editing the message could quietly turn the button into a plain blue link. Drip and blast emails show the same button for estimate, payment, and review links.
howto: Send an estimate or invoice as usual: write your message in the editor and the button is appended for you (a note under the editor confirms it).
You cannot edit or remove the button from the editor; it is fixed per email type so it always renders correctly.
Change order approval emails use the same button and no longer show the long backup link under it.

title: Tickable options in Preview, a cleaner estimate header, and blanks now stop a send
summary: The estimate Preview now works like the real customer page: tick optional items and watch the total, the payment schedule, and the signing amount update live (the accept, change and decline buttons stay disabled, and it is still not sent). The top of the customer estimate is cleaner too: the combined square footage summary is gone because footage lives on each line, and the flake color shows as a short note. And an estimate can no longer be sent, by email, text, or Open for signing in Present mode, while the scope still has an unfilled blank: the word BLANK, an unresolved is/is not choice, or a ____ fill-in. The blocker names the line and quotes the text so you can fix it in one tap.
howto: Tap Preview on any estimate and tick the optional items to demo the price moving before you send.
If a send is blocked, tap the blocker message: it opens that line's editor with the description ready to fix.
When a customer ticks options on their own link, their choices are saved as they go, so you can see where they landed.

title: Sales visit recordings on the customer, pipeline, and estimate, plus a close X on every popup
summary: SalesAsk visit insights now show up where you work: the full recording history on the customer page, a color coded process score chip on each pipeline card, and the latest visit on the estimate page next to pricing. Every popup in the app also has a close X pinned to its top right corner, so a long popup no longer hides its close button.
howto: Open a customer to see every recorded sales visit with its score, summary, action items, coaching notes, and full transcript.
On the pipeline board, look for the SalesAsk score chip on a lead card to see how the visit went at a glance.
Tune the green and amber score thresholds in Settings, under Appointments.

title: Metallic and MVB Only estimates now write their own scope
summary: Dylan approved scope templates for the Metallic and MVB Only systems, so their estimate lines now fill in a full scope of work automatically, the same as Standard Flake. MVB Only lines used to be excused from the scope requirement because no template existed; now they need a scope like every other line before sending, and Generate fills it in one tap.
howto: Price a Metallic or MVB Only area as usual; the scope writes itself on save or when you tap Generate.
You can still tap the line and edit the text; your edit wins until you press Generate again.

title: Tap any estimate line to edit it, including the scope the customer reads
summary: The estimator's line list is a clean table now. Tap a line and a full screen editor opens with its name, price, options, internal notes, and a Description box you can type in. Every line can carry its own scope of work: templates still write it for systems that have one, and for systems that do not (like Custom System) you just type it. One Generate with AI button fills a templated line or cleans up your typed text. If sending is blocked because a line has no scope, the message is now a link: tap it and that line opens with the description ready to type.
howto: Open an estimate, tap Edit, then tap any line in the Line items card to open its editor.
Type the scope in the Description box, or tap Generate with AI to write it from the system template (or clean up what you typed).
If a send is blocked, tap the message in the popup and the blocked line opens with the description focused. Fix it and send again.

title: Open anything in a new tab, and share a link to any screen
summary: Every job row, estimate, lead card, customer, and search result is now a real link. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) and click, or middle click, to open it in a new tab; a plain click works exactly as before. The address bar also follows you around, so you can copy the URL of whatever you are looking at and paste it into Slack, and a signed-in teammate lands on the same record.
howto: Ctrl click (Cmd click on Mac) or middle click any record row, pipeline card, search result, or menu item to open it in a new tab.
To share what you are looking at, copy the URL from the address bar and paste it anywhere; the link opens that exact record.
Back and Forward in the browser still walk through the screens you visited.

title: Know the moment a customer opens their proposal, and spot the hot ones
summary: Every time a customer opens their estimate, a message posts to the #epoxysales Slack channel with who opened it, the price, the salesperson, which open it is, and how long since it was sent. The salesperson on the estimate also gets their own bell notification. The estimate page now shows the full view history (how many times, first and last open, each open listed), and estimates being read repeatedly get a flame on their Sales Pipeline card so you know who to call first.
howto: Watch #epoxysales for the eyes alert whenever a proposal is opened; tap the link in it to jump to the estimate.
On the Sales Pipeline, an eye with a number shows how many times the proposal was opened; a flame means it is hot (repeat views, recently).
Tune what counts as hot, or turn the Slack alert off, in Settings > Estimates.

title: Ordering no longer invents material for change orders
summary: A change order area (like adding striping) no longer generates its own set of material lines, which used to create duplicate topcoat and phantom flake rows on the order sheet. Blank cure speeds now inherit the job's cure speed so the same product merges into one line. If a job's flake color was never picked, the order sheet says Flake color not chosen instead of listing a placeholder you could accidentally order, and the Ordering page has a Refresh button so job card edits made in another tab show up without a full reload.
howto: Open a job with stray duplicate lines and hit Recalculate; the phantom rows are removed as long as they were never marked ordered.
If a job shows the flake color not chosen chip, pick the blend on the job card, then Recalculate.
Use the Refresh button on the Ordering page after editing a job card in another tab.

title: Customer estimates now show the full scope under every line, a payment schedule, and terms
summary: The estimate a customer opens now reads like a full proposal. Every line item shows its complete scope of work right under the line (tap to collapse), with the square footage as a small subtitle. You can set up a payment schedule on the estimate (deposit plus progress payments) that the customer sees and agrees to when signing; percent rows re-balance live as they tick options, and the signed schedule becomes the job's real installments. Your terms and conditions render above the signature, and right after signing the customer can pay their deposit online. Sending is now blocked until every line has real scope and the schedule matches the total, so a half-written estimate can never go out.
howto: In the estimator, use the new Payment schedule card to set the deposit and progress payments; it starts from your default deposit percent.
Write your estimate terms in Settings > Brand under Terms and conditions (estimate); the card only shows once text exists.
If sending is blocked, the message names the exact lines missing scope; Regenerate the scope (or fix the schedule) and send again.

title: New leads get an instant reply, and booking answers land in the right place
summary: When a new lead comes in from the website, TopCoat now sends one fixed thank-you message right away (email always, text only when they gave consent), posts an alert to Slack, and rings the notification bell. The rest of the follow-up drip still waits for your approval like before. Appointment reminders also stop tacking the service picker answer onto the note the customer sees; it goes to the internal note for the rep instead. A new booking link setting drops your Routemize scheduling link into drip messages.
howto: Settings > Drips has the Instant reply switch, the Routemize booking link box, and a readout of how many recent leads arrived with texting consent.
Settings > Appointments > Routemize booking questions controls where each booking form answer goes (customer note, internal note, or dropped).
Drip Approvals works exactly as before for every step after the instant reply.

title: Make any estimate line optional, and keep a record of what the customer passed on
summary: Any line on an estimate can now be optional, not just add-ons. Optional areas and custom lines start ticked for the customer, who can untick them before signing; the total updates live. At least one line always stays required, so an estimate can never be unticked to zero. The estimate stores two numbers, the required floor and the up-to ceiling, and anything the customer declines is kept on the estimate, listed on the job with a one click Add to job at the original quoted price, and noted on the customer card.
howto: In the estimator, tick Optional (customer picks) on any line; use Starts selected to control whether it begins ticked for the customer.
Watch the Required only total and its GP under the price; an amber note warns you if the required lines alone run under your floor.
After a customer declines a line, find it on the job page under Declined options and tap Add to job to sell it later as a change order at the quoted price.

title: The AI price read now checks every line, and comps never mix systems
summary: Comparable jobs are now always the same system as the line you are pricing. If there are no completed jobs on that system, the panel says so instead of borrowing numbers from a different system. The AI price read gives each line its own suggested range and a confidence tag (Comps-backed, Thin sample, or No comps), plus a short read on the whole estimate. A custom line is read from its typed scope and is always marked No comps.
howto: Build an estimate as usual; the AI price read panel now lists each line with its own range and confidence tag.
Green means enough same-system comps back the number; amber means the sample is thin; gray means no comparable jobs exist.
Turn the read on or off, and set the minimum comps sample, in Settings then Estimates under Pricing intelligence.

title: Every estimate line now has its own price, and you can add a custom line to a normal estimate
summary: Each area on an estimate now solves its own price at its own system's target margin, with its own gross profit shown right on the line (red when it drops under the floor). You can also add a custom line, like a stair install or a repair, to the same estimate as your calculator areas: type its label, scope, price, material cost, and crew hours, and it prices and books like every other line. The job discount still works on the whole estimate and spreads across the lines fairly.
howto: In the estimator, tap + Add custom line next to + Add area, then type the label, scope, price, material cost, and crew hours.
To change one line's price, type in that line's Line price box; its gross profit updates on the spot.
Adjust the per-line GP floor and the discount reason thresholds in Settings then Estimates under Line pricing.

title: The work order now shows the BusyBusy clock-in number
summary: The printed crew work order replaces the old DJ number with the Clock in number, which is the BusyBusy project number for the job. New jobs get their BusyBusy project created automatically the moment the customer accepts the estimate, so the number is ready before the crew arrives. Older jobs that only have a DripJobs number still show it.
howto: Open a job and click View Work Order.
The Job Identity box shows Clock in # with the number the crew picks in BusyBusy.
Turn auto-creation on or off, and set the geofence radius, in Settings then BusyBusy under Project auto-create.

title: The Appointments calendar looks like a modern calendar now
summary: Appointment cards follow the Google Calendar style. In Month view each appointment is a soft colored pill showing a type dot, the start time, and the customer's name. In Week and Day view it is a solid colored block showing the name, the visit type, and the city. Colors still mean the same thing: the background is the salesperson, the dot is the appointment type.
howto: Open Appointments from the Sales Activity menu.
Month view shows time and customer name on each pill; Week and Day show more detail in each block.
Everything still works the same: click a card to open it, drag it to reschedule, or drag its bottom edge to change the length.

title: Metrics now has All, Sales, Production, and Admin tabs
summary: The Metrics page can now show just the cards for one part of the business. Pick Sales, Production, or Admin next to the time window buttons, and the page shows only those cards. All shows everything, like before.
howto: Open Metrics from the Overview menu.
Click Sales, Production, or Admin next to the time window buttons.
Click All to see every card again. Your pick sticks until you leave the app.

title: The by-crew Metrics cards now show real crews
summary: Revenue collected, gross profit, and callback rate by crew lead used to lump everything under Unassigned. They now read the crew from the job itself, so Davey, Dylan, Kyle, and Landen each get credit for their own jobs. The callback rate also counts touch-up visits now, charged to the crew that installed the original job.
howto: Open Metrics and scroll to the by-crew cards.
Click any crew row to see the exact jobs and payments behind the number.
Jobs with no crew on the schedule still show under Unassigned; assign a crew on the Job Schedule to fix one.

title: Comps GP% now uses the real job costs
summary: The GP% column in the estimator's comparable jobs panel now uses the same math as Job Costing: materials actually used, crew hours, bonuses, and commission. The old number ignored materials and read about 20 points too high. A comp with no cost data shows a dash instead of a made-up number.
howto: Open an estimate in the estimator and set the system and square footage.
Read the GP% column in the Comparable jobs panel; the line under the table says how many comps have a GP%.
Expect lower numbers than before. Around 59% average is the true figure, not 80%.

title: You can fix the salesperson on your own drafts now
summary: If you started an estimate and the wrong salesperson is on it, you can change it yourself as long as the estimate is still a draft that has not been sent. Once it goes out to the customer, the salesperson is locked and only an admin can change it, because commission follows that name.
howto: Open your draft estimate and change the salesperson in the estimator, or use Edit job info on the estimate page.
Send the estimate only once the right salesperson is on it.
After sending, ask an admin if it still needs to change.

title: One New Estimate form, used everywhere
summary: Starting an estimate now opens a single form no matter where you start from. Pick an existing customer or lead from the Contact dropdown, or fill in a new contact, then add the job address and the salesperson right there. The estimate opens with all of it already filled in. In the side menu, the Pipeline button is now called Sales Pipeline, inside a group called Sales Activity.
howto: Go to Estimates and click New estimate.
Pick a contact from the dropdown, or leave it on New Contact and enter the name and lead source.
Add the job address and check the salesperson, then click Start estimate.

title: Start an estimate straight from an appointment
summary: Open any appointment on the Appointments calendar and click Start estimate. The estimate is created for the appointment's lead or customer, with the appointment's address and the customer's notes carried over. If the appointment is not linked to anyone yet, the New Estimate form opens so you create the customer first.
howto: On the Appointments calendar, click an appointment to open it.
Click Start estimate in the bottom left of the window.
You land on the new estimate with the address and notes already filled in.

title: Appointment notes no longer show ID codes
summary: Notes that came in from online bookings could start with a long ID code instead of the question text, and that code was showing up in the customer's confirmation and reminder messages. New bookings now store just the customer's own words.
howto: Nothing to do. New online bookings come in clean automatically.
Appointments booked before today keep their old notes; you can tidy those by editing the Job notes field on the appointment.

title: Present an estimate on site, and let the customer sign right there
summary: Every estimate now has a Present button that opens a full-screen presentation for the driveway: your company story, how the work happens, photos and reviews, ways to pay, and then the estimate itself. The customer can tick optional add-ons and sign on your tablet, and it counts exactly the same as signing from the emailed link. The same story sections also appear on the customer's estimate page, so whoever was not home can read them later.
howto: Open an estimate and click Present. Use the arrows, the dots, or the dropdown at the top to move between sections.
The last slide is the estimate. Click Open for signing to make it live, then hand the customer your tablet to tick options and sign.
Write and turn on your presentation sections in Settings, Presentation. They ship turned off until you review them.

title: Your sales story lives in Settings now
summary: Settings has a new Presentation tab where you write the sections customers see: why us, our process, a photo gallery with your Google reviews, and financing. Photos are shrunk automatically on upload so pages stay fast on cell data. Four draft sections are already written and waiting for your review; they are turned off until you switch them on.
howto: Go to Settings, Presentation. Edit the four draft sections, add real job photos to the gallery, and click Turn on for each one you want live.
Reorder sections with the arrows; the presentation and the customer page follow this order.
Set how many recent reviews show, and the minimum star rating, at the bottom of the tab.

title: A cleaner estimator: product dropdowns wait until after the sale
summary: The Basecoat, Topcoat, and Flake dropdowns no longer show while you build an estimate. The price already includes standard materials, so nothing changes about the number. Colors and products get picked on the job page after the sale, where they drive ordering and the crew work order. The work order questions stay right where they were. Also fixed: the big blank gap that could appear under the estimator on short estimates.
howto: Build the estimate as usual. You will only see the questions that matter during the sale.
If a job needs a product spec now (a commercial bid, or a customer who already picked a color), click Specify products in the Products and colors card to show the dropdowns.
After the job is sold, pick the flake color and products on the job page's line items, then order materials as usual.

title: The estimate preview can be closed now
summary: The Preview window on an estimate used to have no close button, and the only way out was reloading the page. It now has a header with the estimate number and an X, and it also closes with the Escape key or a click outside the window. Forms like payments and change orders still require their own Cancel button, so a stray click cannot wipe what you typed.
howto: Open an estimate and click Preview to see exactly what the customer will get.
Close it with the X in the corner, the Escape key, or a click anywhere outside the window.

title: One search box finds everything
summary: The search bar at the top of the page now searches jobs, estimates, leads, and customers at the same time, from any page. Results are grouped by type, and clicking one takes you straight to that record. The small search boxes inside each list still work as before; they narrow down the list you are looking at, while the top bar jumps you to a record.
howto: Type a name, phone number, address, or estimate number (102026 or EST-102026 both work) into the search bar at the top.
Click a result to open that job, estimate, lead, or customer.
Click +N more under a group to see the full filtered list for that type.

title: Leads can be a business or a person, like customers
summary: The New lead form now asks whether the lead is an individual or a business, the same way the customer form does. A person needs a first and last name; a business needs the business name, with an optional contact person. You can also fix a lead's name later with the pencil button on the lead page.
howto: On New lead, pick Individual or Business at the top and fill in the matching name fields.
To change a name later, open the lead and click the pencil next to the name.

title: Archive dead leads without deleting them
summary: Archiving clears a lead off the pipeline board and stops all automatic follow-ups, but keeps the contact and its full history. The lead's stage does not change; an archived lead is not the same as a lost one. Find archived leads any time with the Show: Archived filter on the board, and unarchive with one click.
howto: Click Archive on a lead card or at the top of the lead page, and confirm.
To bring one back, set the Show filter on the pipeline board to Archived and click Unarchive.

title: Drafts on the pipeline, and estimates without a lead
summary: Starting an estimate now offers three paths: pick an existing customer, pick an existing lead, or create a new customer on the spot. An estimate does not need a lead anymore. The pipeline board gained a Drafts column showing started estimates that have not been sent, and estimates without a lead appear as their own cards that move with the estimate itself (send it and the card moves to Estimate Sent). Lead cards with a draft in progress show a small Draft chip.
howto: Click New estimate on the Estimates page and choose Existing customer, From a lead, or New customer.
Watch the Drafts column between Estimate Scheduled and Estimate Sent for anything started but not sent.
Estimate cards cannot be dragged; open the estimate and send, present, or accept it to move the card.

title: Lost leads: notes plus a suggested reason from the last call
summary: Marking a lead lost now has a notes box you can always use, alongside the required reason. If the lead has a recent phone call on record, TopCoat pre-selects the closest reason and pre-fills the notes from the call summary, showing you the source; you can change both before saving. A nightly pass also fills in reasons for old lost leads that never got one, and anything filled automatically is tagged on the lead's timeline so you can tell it apart from what a person typed.
howto: Drag a lead to Lost (or pick Lost in the stage dropdown), check the suggested reason, adjust the notes, and click Mark lost.
Turn the nightly auto-fill on or off in Settings under Drips.

title: Estimator: everything visible, one crew notes box, loud reminder for site readings
summary: The collapsed More detail section is gone; products, colors, and the site questions are always on screen. Special notes merged into the big Notes for the crew box at the bottom, which is what prints on the crew work order. If moisture or MOHS hardness is blank, a red banner appears on the estimator and the estimate page reminding you the work order will print blank. It is a reminder only; saving and sending always work.
howto: Scroll the estimate form; the products, colors, and site questions are right there, no section to expand.
Put anything the crew needs to know in the Notes for the crew box at the bottom.
When you see the red banner, fill in moisture and MOHS under Work order and it goes away.

title: The estimator now lives on the estimate page, and job info is editable right there
summary: No more popup window. Starting an estimate creates it immediately and opens its own page with the estimator built in; a draft opens ready to work, and Edit on a sent estimate swaps the estimator in on the same page. Saving keeps you where you are, with the header and totals refreshing in place. The customer and job info block is now editable without opening the estimator at all, and when you change something that also lives on the lead or customer, TopCoat asks whether to update them too (your choice each time). If you are offline, the classic window still works and saves to the device.
howto: Click Start estimate on a lead (or New estimate): you land on the new estimate's page with the estimator open and the customer info already filled in.
To fix just a phone number or address, use Edit job info on the estimate page. Tick or untick the boxes when asked about updating the lead and customer.
Close inside the estimator to see the read-only summary; Edit brings the estimator back. Nothing you typed is lost when totals refresh.

title: Lead sources are one list now, and you can change them anytime
summary: Lead sources used to be set once at creation and written in two different vocabularies. Now one managed list (Settings, Lead sources) drives everything: the leads board, the customer list, and what the intake feeds write. Click the source badge on a lead (or the source line on a customer) to change it; the linked record updates with it and the change is recorded on the lead's timeline with who made it. New feed spellings can be mapped from Settings with the new Aliases field, no code change needed.
howto: Open a lead and click its source badge, pick the right source, Save. The linked customer updates too.
Same thing from a customer page: click the source line next to the brand badge.
To map a new feed's spelling, open Settings, Lead sources, Edit, and add the raw token to Aliases (comma separated).

title: Google review requests and a crew leader review scoreboard
summary: When you mark a job complete, TopCoat now asks whether to send the customer a Google review request (Send is preselected, Skip is one click). The customer gets a short text the next day with a one tap review link, then a gentle follow up on days 3, 7 and 14 that stops the moment they review, reply, or a touch up opens. Reviews from Google flow into the rebuilt Reviews view, where confirming a match credits the crew leader and queues their review bonus. Metrics has a new Reviews section with the ask funnel and a per crew leader scoreboard. Every message currently waits in Drip Approvals for a human OK before it sends.
howto: Mark a job complete anywhere and choose Send request in the popup (or Skip; you can start it later from the job with the Request review button).
When a review arrives, open Reviews and click Confirm match if the suggested job is right. That is what credits the crew leader and creates the bonus.
Tune everything under Settings, Reviews: the bonus amount, the popup default, and the bad review alert threshold.

title: The Leads board is now Sales Pipeline, with a new Estimate Scheduled column
summary: The left menu item that used to say Leads now says Pipeline, under a Sales Pipeline group. The board itself gained a seventh column, Estimate Scheduled, between Contacted and Estimate Sent. It fills itself when an on-site estimate appointment is booked and the lead moves back to Contacted if that appointment is canceled. Cards in it show the visit date and the column sorts soonest visit first.
howto: Open Sales Pipeline, then Pipeline in the left menu (your old Leads bookmark still works).
Book an estimate with the Schedule Estimate button on a lead card and the lead moves to Estimate Scheduled on its own.
You can also drag a card in or out of the column by hand, like any other stage.

title: Older jobs keep their original labor numbers
summary: A recent update made Job Costing calculate labor from crew hours. On 34 older jobs that had both a typed labor cost and hand-entered hours, the calculated number quietly replaced the typed one and shifted their profit. Per Dylan's ruling, those jobs now keep the labor cost that was typed in, so their history reads exactly as it did before. New jobs, and any job with BusyBusy clock hours, still use the automatic math.
howto: Nothing to do. Open Job Costing and older jobs show their original typed Salary and Wages again.
Jobs with BusyBusy hours keep the automatic labor math, including the 25% burden.

title: Financing option on estimates and invoices
summary: Customers can now see a financing option right on the public estimate page, the estimate PDF, and the public invoice page. When an APR and term are set in Settings, the block shows an estimated monthly payment (clearly labeled an estimate, subject to credit approval); otherwise it shows a simple check-your-options button. Nothing appears anywhere until you turn it on, and jobs under your minimum amount never show it.
howto: Open Settings, General, and find the Financing (Enhancify) section.
Paste the Enhancify apply link (and embed URL if you have one), set the minimum job total, and switch the block On.
Optionally set an APR and term to quote an estimated monthly payment; leave them blank to show just the button.

title: Work order questions on custom estimates, plus a moisture and MOHS reminder
summary: Custom estimates now ask the same work order questions as standard ones (gate code, moisture, MOHS, tooling, and the rest), so the crew sheet is complete either way. And when Moisture or MOHS hardness is left blank, the estimator and the job page both show a gentle reminder. It never blocks anything: you can still save, send, and accept as always.
howto: In the estimator's Custom mode, open the new Work order (site questions) section and fill in what you know.
If Moisture or MOHS is blank, a yellow note appears near Save and on the job page until it is filled in.
Fill in the reading on the job page (Job Card) whenever you get it; the warning goes away on its own.

title: The schedule now shows each job's real price
summary: Calendar bars, week revenue totals, Next Day cards, run sheets, and the schedule window now show the job's current estimate total, including change orders, instead of the original booking number. If the estimate changes, the schedule follows automatically. Jobs already completed or finalized keep the numbers they always showed, and manually added jobs still use the price you typed.
howto: Add a change order or edit an estimate, then reload the schedule: the price updates everywhere at once.
Hover a calendar bar to see where the number comes from and what the job was originally booked at.
In the schedule window, a price that comes from the estimate is read-only; change it on the job page instead.

title: Change orders are spelled out on the job page and the crew work order
summary: Every change order now shows itemized on the job detail page, including ones that never got a signature link, with a total that matches the Totals card. The printed work order gains a CHANGE ORDERS section on page 1, right by the scope, so the crew sees added work on the page they actually read instead of a back-page footnote.
howto: Open a job with change orders: each one lists its name, details, amount, and signature status, with a total underneath.
Print the work order: added scope shows on page 1 with sqft and price.
Jobs without change orders look exactly the same as before.

title: Calendars now start the week on Sunday
summary: The Job Schedule week and 3-week views, the Next Day window, and the date pickers all start on Sunday now, matching a normal American calendar. One thing to know: the per-week revenue totals group by the new week boundary, so a Sunday install now counts in the week it starts rather than the week before. Metrics and weekly charts are unchanged.
howto: Open the Job Schedule: every grid starts on Sunday.
If a week's revenue total looks different from last week's report, check whether a Sunday job moved weeks; that is the new boundary, not a data change.

title: Touch-up count now includes scheduled work
summary: The Touch-ups panel header on the Job Schedule now counts everything still owed to a customer: open, waiting, and scheduled touch-ups together, labeled outstanding. Before, a touch-up dropped out of the count the moment it was scheduled, so the header could read zero while work was still owed. The Open and Scheduled sections inside the panel are unchanged.
howto: Open the Job Schedule and look at the Touch-ups header: the number now means not done yet.
Expand the panel to see the same Open and Scheduled split as before.

title: Ordering reworked: pick the jobs, then order exactly what they need
summary: The Ordering page now starts with a Jobs to order list showing each open job's scheduled dates, crew, system, and whether colors are confirmed. Check the jobs you want to buy for and the Order sheet below builds the shopping list from just those jobs, grouped by supplier with costs. You can edit any quantity right on the sheet and your number sticks, even through a recalculate, until you reset it. You can also add extra materials to a job or remove ones you added by hand. One note: quantities you hand-edited before this update will refresh to the calculated amount the next time that job is recalculated; edit them once more and they will stick from then on.
howto: Open Ordering and check the boxes next to the jobs you want to order material for.
In the Order sheet, type over any quantity to override it. The pencil mark shows it is yours; reset brings back the calculated number.
Use + Add line on a selected job for extra material, and Print order for a supplier-ready sheet.

title: Routemize bookings now land on the TopCoat calendar
summary: Appointments booked through Routemize flow straight into TopCoat. Each booking shows on the Appointments calendar with the right time, salesperson, and the customer's own form answers, and it syncs out to Google Calendar like any other appointment. If the booker is brand new, TopCoat creates the lead for them automatically so follow-up never misses them, and a repeat customer is matched to their existing record instead of duplicated.
howto: Open Appointments to see Routemize bookings appear automatically (source: Routemize).
Open Settings, then Appointments, then Routemize booking intake to map each Routemize service name to an appointment type.
Anything not mapped comes in as an on-site estimate, so new services still land safely.

title: SalesAsk sales visit recordings are wired in
summary: In-home sales appointments now sync to SalesAsk automatically, and the recording your rep makes there flows back with its AI summary, action items, and coaching score. Recordings show on the lead timeline, the customer profile, and the appointment itself, and the lead AI reads what was actually said in the visit. Metrics also gains a Sales coaching card: recordings per rep, average process score, coverage, and close rate split by process score.
howto: Open Settings, Appointments, and turn on SalesAsk recording sync (enter each rep's SalesAsk login email below the switch).
Book appointments like normal; they appear in the rep's SalesAsk app so the recording attaches itself.
After the visit, open the lead or customer to see the recording summary, or click Listen to hear it in SalesAsk.
Open Metrics and find the Sales coaching card in the Sales section to compare reps and see whether followed process closes more jobs.

title: Schedule bars are colored by crew
summary: Calendar bars, Next Day cards, and the printed run sheet now fill with the crew's color, so you can see who is where at a glance. The system type still shows as a thin band along the top of each bar, and a color key sits above the calendar. Touch-ups keep their sky blue.
howto: Open Settings, General, and click a crew to pick its color.
Open the Job Schedule; each crew's jobs share one fill color and the key above the calendar names them.
The thin band on top of a bar is the system type, same as the old bar color.

title: One job popup, from every schedule surface
summary: Clicking a calendar bar, a Next Day card, or a Pending card now opens the same read-only job popup. It shows more too: crew, scheduled dates, customer phone, square footage, flake and coating picks, and a TOUCHUP badge. The Schedule button inside it is the way into the edit form, so a stray click can no longer land you in an editable schedule.
howto: Click any job bar on the Job Schedule or any card on the Next Day board.
Read the details; call the customer straight from the phone link.
Click Schedule inside the popup when you actually want to change the schedule. Dragging a Next Day card still moves it without opening anything.

title: Bank transfers in progress show on the job invoice
summary: When a customer starts an ACH bank transfer, the job invoice now says so instead of looking unpaid. The Due now amount gains a small note that a transfer is clearing, the payment schedule marks the installment it covers, and the Payments list shows the pending transfer with its start date and when to expect it. Nothing is counted as paid until the bank actually settles it.
howto: Open the job's invoice from Invoicing.
Look under Due now for the bank transfer clearing note, and in Payments for the pending row.
No need to chase the customer; transfers clear in 3 to 5 business days. If one fails it shows in red with the reason.

title: One standard flake product, colors picked per job
summary: The 18 identically priced Torginol flake colors are becoming one Standard Flake product, with the blend chosen from a color list that also carries each blend's basecoat pairing. Obsidian, Autumn Brown, and Stonewash stay separate because their cost or coverage differs. Old jobs keep their original colors and prices. This switches on once the database migration is applied.
howto: Build a job with a flake system; the Flake color dropdown lists every blend by name.
Pick a blend; the right basecoat pairs up automatically.
In the Catalog, retired flake products hide behind the Show inactive checkbox.

title: People and Users are one tab now
summary: Settings has one People tab where each person is one record: identity, roles, wage and commission, and now their login too. Open a person to set their role and permissions or reset their password, and use Create login for someone who does not have one. The recent sign-ins list moved to the bottom of the People tab.
howto: Open Settings, People, and click Edit on a person.
Use the Login section to set role and permissions, reset the password, or create a login.
Changes take effect the next time that person loads the app.

title: BusyBusy times read like a clock
summary: Punch times in the BusyBusy import preview and its anomaly messages now show as 7:15 am or 3:42 pm instead of 24-hour times.
howto: Open Settings, BusyBusy, and fetch a preview.
Times in the anomaly table and messages read in am/pm.

title: Settings tabs fit on small windows
summary: The Settings tab row scrolls sideways instead of cutting off the last tabs on a narrow window, and the active tab scrolls into view on its own.
howto: Open Settings on a small window or split screen.
Swipe or scroll the tab row sideways to reach every tab.

title: Job costing now counts crew labor
summary: Hours imported from BusyBusy turn into a real labor cost on the job costing card, so gross profit and GP per hour finally reflect what the job actually cost. The Salary and Wages field fills in automatically from crew hours and wages (including the labor burden), the suggested crew bonus counts against profit as pending, and you approve that bonus with one click, right under the number it is based on. The manual bonus section is gone; the $50 crew lead bonus checkbox moved onto the Labor and Bonus Payout card.
howto: Open a job in Job Costing and expand Labor and Bonus Payout.
Check the crew hours and the suggested bonus, then click Approve.
Gross profit at the top of the card now includes labor and the approved bonus.

title: The scheduler fills in system type and estimated hours for you
summary: Scheduling a job used to start with a blank System type and blank Estimated hours, even when the estimate already knew both. Now the schedule popup, the Pending Jobs cards, the calendar bars, and the Next Day board all read the job's estimate and show its system and hours automatically, the same numbers Job Costing uses. Both fields stay editable: type your own hours and your number wins on the schedule, and if the estimate later disagrees the popup shows what the estimate now says with a one-click Use it. Picking a system in the popup makes that choice stick; leaving it alone keeps following the estimate.
howto: Open Job Schedule and click + Schedule on a pending job. System type and Estimated hours arrive pre-filled from the estimate.
Type over the hours to override them for scheduling. Job Costing and crew bonus keep using the estimate's number.
Pick a different system only if the estimate is wrong; your pick sticks from then on.

title: Salesperson is locked in at the estimate and shown everywhere
summary: The salesperson on an estimate is now set when the estimate is started and can only be changed by an admin afterward, which protects commission tracking. The job page shows the salesperson (admins can change it there, and the change is recorded in the job's activity log), and the printed work order now lists the salesperson in its Job Identity section. A job with nobody assigned shows Unassigned and appears on the new Ops Queue so it gets fixed.
howto: Open any job to see its salesperson in the header. Admins can change it right there.
Print a work order: the salesperson appears under Job Identity.
Reps whose login is not yet linked to a sales team member can still pick a name when starting an estimate.

title: New Ops Queue: everything that needs a human, on one screen
summary: Admins get a new Ops Queue view (Overview group) that scans the live data for anything stalled or incomplete: unmapped BusyBusy names, costings waiting to be finalized, scheduled jobs with no revenue, completed jobs never invoiced, jobs missing a salesperson or a system, drips held for approval, touch-ups open too long, deposits not collected, and system health. Every row links straight to the screen where it gets fixed. You can also add your own items, assign them to a teammate with a due date, and mark them done; new manual items ring the bell and show a count on the nav button. Each check can be switched off and its thresholds adjusted in Settings, General tab.
howto: Open Ops Queue in the Overview group of the nav.
Click Open on any row to jump to the screen that fixes it, or Dismiss to hide that one item for good.
Use + Add item to assign a task to a teammate, with an optional due date. It appears with a badge on the nav and a bell notification.

title: One People directory, with team birthdays
summary: Team members, sales reps, and CRM users used to live in separate lists, so the same person could appear three times. The new Settings, People tab shows every person once, with badges for the roles they hold (Login, Sales, Crew), their crew assignment, hourly wage, commission rate, and birthday, all editable in one place. Edits flow through to the old lists automatically, so nothing else changes. Birthdays are month and day only (no year, no age anywhere), and the app reminds everyone a week ahead with a dashboard banner and a bell notification. Reminder timing is adjustable in Settings, General tab.
howto: Open Settings and click the People tab to see everyone in one list.
If the same person shows up twice from the old lists, use the Possible duplicates card to merge them (or keep them separate).
Click Edit on a row to set a birthday. New people require one; existing people are listed in a reminder until theirs is set.

title: Attach data sheets and safety sheets to catalog products
summary: Every product in the Price & Material Catalog can now carry two PDFs: the manufacturer's data sheet (TDS) and its safety sheet (MSDS/SDS). Attach them in the product editor and they show up as TDS and SDS chips on the catalog list, where clicking a chip opens the PDF. On a job page, a Data sheets button appears next to View Work Order whenever that job's materials actually have sheets attached, and it lists every sheet for the job in one place. The links are public PDFs, so they can be texted or printed for the crew without a login. The maximum upload size is adjustable in Settings, General tab.
howto: Open Production, Price & Material Catalog, and click a product to edit it.
In the Data sheets section, pick a PDF for the TDS or the MSDS/SDS. It uploads right away; then press Save.
On a job whose materials have sheets, click the Data sheets button next to View Work Order to see them all.

title: The work order now prints job, crew, and date big at the top
summary: The printed crew work order replaces the small Crew Work Order title with three large boxes: Job, Crew, and Date. They are the biggest text on the sheet, so anyone can tell whose job it is and who runs it at a glance. If the job is not on the calendar yet, the Crew and Date boxes print empty with room to write them in by hand, matching how the rest of the sheet is filled out on paper. The small Crew, Date, and Job Name rows lower on the sheet were removed because the same facts now print once, large.
howto: Open a job and click View Work Order.
The Job, Crew, and Date boxes are at the top, next to the logo. Print as usual.

title: Real crew hours now flow into job costing from BusyBusy
summary: Job costing no longer waits on hand-typed crew hours.
