A new BusyBusy tab in Settings pulls the crew's actual punches for a date window, shows you exactly what came back (total hours, overtime, shop time, hours per job, and anything odd like a forgotten clock-out), and imports only when you press Import. Pulling the same window again after a punch is corrected in BusyBusy is safe and normal, the import replaces those dates cleanly. Each BusyBusy worker name is matched to a team member once on the same tab (salespeople can be ignored), and each BusyBusy project links to a job once, then stays linked. Overtime lands on whichever job the person was on when they passed 40 hours for the week, matching payroll exactly. Shop time is tracked as overhead and never charges a job. Jobs with imported hours use them automatically in the bonus math; manual hour entry still works for anything BusyBusy does not cover.
howto: Open Settings and pick the BusyBusy tab. The date window is prefilled with the last two full weeks.
Press Fetch preview and read the summary. Map any unmapped names and link any unlinked projects right below.
Press Import. The hours appear on each job's costing page and drive the crew bonus automatically.

title: Touch-ups now have their own list on the Job Schedule
summary: Touch-up and warranty visits no longer hide among Pending Jobs. The Job Schedule has a new Touch-ups panel that tracks each one from the moment a customer calls to the day it is closed out. Add one right from the panel by searching the original job, or from the job's page. Drag to set the order you want to work them, or tap Sort by suggested to rank by who has an active job, where crews already are, and how long it has been waiting. Rows turn red when a touch-up sits open too long (14 days by default, adjustable in Settings). Closing one asks why it happened, and the Report link totals those causes by crew so you can see what is driving callbacks. Scheduled touch-ups show a TOUCHUP tag on the Next Day board and the printed run sheet, at zero dollars unless you mark one billable.
howto: Open Job Schedule. The Touch-ups panel sits above Pending Jobs on the left.
Tap + Touch-up and search the customer's name or address to log a new one, then + Schedule on its row when you are ready to book it.
When the work is done, tap Close on the row and pick the cause. Tap Report in the panel header to see totals by cause and crew.

title: Metrics: pick your time window (MTD, YTD, 4 weeks, custom) and get an AI read of it
summary: The Metrics tab now opens to Month to date, with one-tap buttons for Year to date, Last 4 weeks, or a Custom date range. The window you pick drives everything on the tab, including the charts, the Sales section, and every drill-down. At the top there is a new AI insights panel: tap Generate insights and it writes a short plain-language read of what moved in the selected window and what to act on. It only runs when you tap the button, and it remembers the last read per window so repeat taps are instant.
howto: Open Metrics and tap MTD, YTD, Last 4 weeks, or Custom at the top left.
For Custom, pick a From and To date and tap Apply.
Tap Generate insights in the AI insights panel for a written summary of the window you are looking at. Tap Regenerate for a fresh one.

title: Job costing: a cleaner page and a new Office notes box
summary: The job costing detail now opens to a compact summary (revenue, costs, gross profit, bonus pool) with each section folded up below it. Tap a section header to open just what you need; the totals still show on the closed headers. There is also a new Office notes box in the Notes section, separate from the regular notes, for things like billing quirks or customer conversations. It shows who wrote the note and when.
howto: Open a job from Job Costing. The profit summary is at the top; tap any section header (Materials, Costs, Notes, and so on) to open it.
To leave an office note, open the Notes section and type in the Office notes box. It saves when you click away.
The name and time under the box show who last updated it.

title: Crew bonuses now wait 14 days after job completion before they can be paid
summary: This is on purpose, payroll is not broken. A bonus becomes payable 14 days after the job's completion date, so any callback has time to surface first. The Bonus Report shows each waiting bonus with its unlock date. If a job gets a callback visit, its bonuses are held for a manual decision: pay in full, reduce, or void, with a required reason. Admins also get a Reverse button on paid bonuses to claw one back with a reason on record, without deleting any history.
howto: Open Bonus Report. Locked bonuses show their payable date; they cannot be selected until then.
If a row says Callback review needed, choose Pay full, Reduce, or Void.
If a row says Completion date missing, use Set completion date on it so the clock can start.

title: Turn on two-factor sign-in for your account
summary: You can now add a second step to your login for extra security. There is a new shield button at the top right, next to the logout button. Tap it, scan the code with an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Authy, or 1Password), and enter the 6-digit code to turn it on. After that, each time you sign in you will enter a fresh code from the app. This is optional for now, but recommended. You can turn it back off from the same shield button.
howto: Tap the shield button at the top right of the screen.
Scan the square code with an authenticator app on your phone, then type the 6-digit code it shows and tap Turn on 2FA.
Next time you sign in, enter the current 6-digit code from that app when asked.

title: The estimator now tells you clearly when a save is not uploading
summary: Before, a save that kept failing to upload only showed as a small 'to sync' counter, which looked like normal progress. Now, if a save fails to upload twice, the top of the estimator turns red and says how many saves are stuck and for how long. Your work is not lost. It is saved on your phone and keeps retrying on its own, and the office is notified automatically. The red banner is just telling you the office has not received it yet.
howto: If you see a red 'saves not syncing' banner, tap it to see what is stuck and why.
Tap Retry now if you think the problem is fixed (for example, you are back on good signal).
If it stays red, tell Dylan and read him the error message shown under the stuck item.

title: Estimates save as an In Draft card the moment you start, and default to you as the salesperson
summary: When you start a new estimate from a lead, the estimate now appears in the Estimates list as an In Draft card as soon as you make your first edit, so nothing is lost if you get pulled away before hitting Save. New estimates also pick you as the salesperson automatically (based on your login), instead of whoever happened to be first in the list. You can still change the salesperson freely, for example when creating an estimate for another rep. If your login is not linked to a salesperson yet, the estimator tells you and an admin can link it in Settings under Sales Team.
howto: Start an estimate from a lead as usual; after your first edit, look in the Estimates list and you will see it there with an In Draft label.
Check the Salesperson box on a new estimate: it should already show your name. Change it any time you are estimating on someone else's behalf.
Admins: open Settings, then Sales Team, edit a member, and set their Login so the automatic salesperson pick works for them.

title: Add an extra coat (like MVB) to a job as a change order
summary: The change order window on a job has a new Additional coat option. Pick the coat (moisture vapor barrier for now) and the area it goes on; the square footage fills in from that area and a suggested price appears, which you can edit freely. You can even set the price to zero dollars to absorb the coat as an internal cost with no customer charge (the screen tells you this lowers the job's profit). Saving adds the product to the job's material pull and job costing automatically, just like any other change order.
howto: Open the job and click Add change order, then choose the Additional coat tab.
Pick MVB and the area it goes on; adjust the square footage or price if needed (zero dollars means no customer charge).
Save. The material shows up on the material pull and job costing on its own, and any price you set is added to the invoice.

title: The left menu is reorganized into clearer groups
summary: The sidebar now has dedicated groups for Leads (with Appointments), Estimates, and Drips, so those no longer hide inside Sales. Jobs pipeline moved into Production next to the schedules, and Settings, Pricing, and Sync Health live in a new Settings group at the bottom. Every page works exactly as before; only where you find it changed.
howto: Look for Leads, Estimates, and Drips as their own icons in the left rail.
Find Jobs pipeline under Production.
Find Settings, Pricing, and Sync Health under the new Settings group.

title: See when a customer opens their estimate
summary: Every time a customer opens their estimate link, TopCoat records it and drops a notification in the bell so the whole team knows there is interest. Clicking the notification opens that estimate, and the estimate card now shows how many times it was viewed and when it was last opened. Automatic link previews from text and email apps are filtered out so the bell only rings for real opens.
howto: Send an estimate like normal; when the customer opens it, a bell notification appears for everyone.
Click the notification to jump straight to that estimate.
Check the bottom of the Customer view card on any estimate for the view count; tune the notification switches in Settings > Estimates.

title: The estimator now finds existing customers so you never create duplicates
summary: When you start an estimate, a search box at the top of the customer form looks up existing customers and leads as you type a name, phone number, email, or address. Each result is labeled Customer or Lead with its phone and address so you can tell people apart. Picking one fills in the whole customer form and attaches the estimate to that existing record, so follow-ups, appointments, and history all stay on one card instead of splitting across duplicates. The search needs a connection; offline estimating works exactly as before.
howto: Start a new estimate and type into Search existing customers and leads at the top of the customer form.
Pick the right match; the form fills in and a note confirms the estimate is linked to that record.
Not the right person after all? Click Unlink and type the details by hand. The search can be turned off in Settings > Estimates.

title: Required deposits, partial invoicing, and payment schedules
summary: You are no longer limited to billing the full project total. When an estimate is accepted, a deposit is prepared automatically at your default percent (you still send it yourself). On any invoice you can build a payment schedule: each installment is a dollar amount or a percent of the total, due on a job milestone (acceptance, job start, or completion). Only one amount is ever due at a time; the customer's pay page shows the amount due now plus the whole plan, and paying online charges exactly that amount. When a milestone happens, the installment waits in Approvals for your OK before anything sends, and payment reminders talk about the amount currently due instead of the whole balance. Invoices without a schedule work exactly as before.
howto: Open an invoice and click Build schedule to add installments (dollars or percent, each tied to a milestone), or Prepare deposit to add just the deposit.
Send the deposit with the normal Send control; milestone installments appear in Approvals when they come due and send after you approve them.
Tune the company default deposit percent and the schedule switches in Settings > Invoicing (a system type can carry its own deposit percent in the catalog).

title: Drip Approvals: review and OK every automatic message before it sends
summary: While the new approval setting is on, every automatic follow-up message (lead, estimate, and invoice drips) waits in the Drip Approvals page instead of sending on its own. You see the exact text or email, can edit it, and then Approve and Send, Skip that step, or Stop the drip for that person. If the customer replied, paid, or opted out while a message was waiting, approving it will not send; the item is closed with the reason shown. Texts approved outside the send window go out when the window opens.
howto: Open Drip Approvals in the left menu to see everything waiting.
Read the message, tweak the wording if you want, then click Approve and Send.
Use Skip this step to move on without sending, or Stop drip to end that person's follow-ups.

title: Drip controls now live in Settings
summary: Settings has a new Drips tab with the three controls that matter: the master on/off switch for all automatic sending (the same one as on the Drips page), the approval switch that decides whether messages wait for a human OK first, and the send window (start time, end time, and days) that texts are allowed to go out in. Changing the window needs no code change and applies to drips and blasts right away; a text due outside the window waits for the next opening instead of being skipped.
howto: Go to Settings, then the Drips tab.
Use the top switch to pause or resume all automatic sending in one click.
Adjust the send window times and days and click Save window; emails still send any time.

title: Appointments booked in Routemize show up on the calendar by themselves
summary: When a customer books through Routemize, the appointment now lands on the TopCoat Appointments calendar automatically, assigned to the right salesperson and linked to the matching lead. The customer gets the usual booking confirmation text and email, the lead moves to Contacted, and its automatic follow-up messages stop so nobody gets a follow-up text after they already booked. Cancel or reschedule in Routemize and the calendar updates too.
howto: Book, move, or cancel appointments in Routemize like normal; TopCoat mirrors it within a few seconds.
Open the Appointments view to see them; Routemize bookings look like any other appointment.
If a booking could not be matched to a lead or salesperson, the details are in the appointment's Company notes so you can link or assign it.

title: Jobs only count as complete when you mark them complete
summary: A job used to flip to completed by itself the day after its last scheduled day, which put jobs into the AR list that were not really done (or that got new days added later). Now a job that runs past its schedule simply stays in progress until someone hits Mark Complete, so the Completed, not paid in full list only shows work a person confirmed is finished. Jobs that show completed but still have days on the calendar now sit in their own section on the Invoicing tab and no longer count toward Total AR.
howto: Finish a job? Mark it complete from the job page, the Invoicing tab, or by dragging it to Complete on the pipeline.
Nothing else changes it to completed for you, so Total AR is only work that is truly done.
Check the Completed, but still on the schedule section on the Invoicing tab for older jobs parked out of AR.

title: New Ready to invoice list on the Invoicing tab
summary: Since jobs no longer complete themselves, finished work could sit unnoticed if nobody marks it complete. The new Ready to invoice section catches it: any in progress job whose last scheduled day has passed shows up there with its balance and a Mark Complete button. One click confirms the job is done and moves it into the Completed list so you can send the final invoice.
howto: Open the Invoicing tab and look at Ready to invoice (work finished, not marked complete).
Hit Mark Complete on a job that is really done; it moves into the Completed, not paid in full list.
Send the final invoice from there like always.

title: See today at a glance when scheduling, and tap a job name for a quick look
summary: The month day pickers in the Schedule and Add Job windows now outline today's date, so you can orient yourself before picking install days. And the job name is now clickable on both the Pending Jobs list and the Next Day board: tap it to open the quick summary card with the proposal, price, system, hours, and scope. Dragging cards on the Next Day board works exactly like before.
howto: Open + Schedule on any pending job, or open Add Job: today's date has a ring around it.
Click a job's name in Pending Jobs or on the Next Day board to see its summary.
Use + Schedule inside the summary to jump straight to scheduling.

title: Job site photos while you schedule, with zoom
summary: The Schedule window now has a Site photos section showing the job's CompanyCam photos, so you can check the site while picking days and crews. Open any photo full screen and zoom in for a closer look: double click or scroll to magnify, drag to move around, pinch on a phone. The same zoom works in the job page photo gallery. If the job has no CompanyCam project linked yet, a Link a project button takes you to the job page to set it up.
howto: Open + Schedule on a job and expand Site photos (CompanyCam).
Click a photo to open it full screen, then double click or scroll to zoom and drag to look around.
Double click again to zoom back out, then swipe or use the arrows for the next photo.

title: Appointments now have customer Job notes and internal Company notes
summary: The appointment form has two note boxes instead of one. Job notes are what the customer sees: they are added to the automated confirmation and reminder texts and emails, so you can say things like please clear the garage before we arrive. Company notes are private: they show on the salesperson's Google Calendar event, along with the customer's name, phone number, and a link that opens the appointment in TopCoat, and are never sent to the customer.
howto: Open an appointment (or book a new one) from the Appointments page.
Put anything the customer should know in Job notes, and private detail in Company notes.
Save. Reminders carry the Job notes; the Google event carries the Company notes.

title: Customer phone numbers on job, lead, and appointment pages
summary: The customer's phone number now shows on the job page, the lead card and lead page, the appointment popup, and the printed crew work order. Tap the number to call. Tap Text next to it to open the existing texting screen for that person, so opt-outs and message history all stay in one place. On the job page, Text opens that job's own Messages and Calls feed.
howto: Open a job, a lead, or an appointment.
Tap the phone number to call, or tap Text to send a message.
If there is no phone on file, it says so instead of showing a dead link.

title: One Send button for invoices and estimates, by email and text together
summary: Invoices and estimates now have a single Send button. Clicking it sends by email and text together: you still write the email in the compose window and confirm the text before anything goes out, so nothing sends by accident. The small arrow next to it offers Email only or Text only. Texting an estimate is brand new: the customer gets a text with their review-and-sign link, and the estimate is marked sent just like an emailed one. If the customer only has an email or only a phone, whatever is on file sends and a note tells you what was skipped.
howto: Open an invoice or an estimate and click Send.
Confirm the text and finish the email compose window.
Use the arrow next to Send for Email only or Text only.

title: New Appointments calendar for sales visits
summary: There is a new Appointments page under Sales. It is a Month, Week, and Day calendar for on-site estimates, project walkthroughs, site visits, and other blocks like a supply run. Each appointment is assigned to a salesperson and gets that person's color, with a second color stripe for the appointment type. Filter by type or by salesperson (All Users shows everyone), drag an appointment to reschedule it, or drag its edge to change the length.
howto: Open Appointments under Sales in the left menu.
Click New Appointment, or click a day or time slot on the calendar, to book one.
Click any appointment to edit, cancel, or delete it, and drag it to reschedule.

title: Schedule an estimate straight from a lead
summary: Leads now have a Schedule Estimate button, on the lead card and on the lead page. It opens the appointment form already filled in with the customer's name and address, books it on the Appointments calendar, and moves a brand-new lead to Contacted. When it is booked, the assigned salesperson gets a bell notification and the customer gets a confirmation text and email (only if they have agreed to be contacted). A reminder also goes out the day before; you can change the timing and wording in Settings.
howto: Open Leads and find the lead.
Click Schedule Estimate on the card or at the top of the lead page.
Pick the date, time, and salesperson, then click Book it.

title: Connect your Google Calendar to Appointments
summary: Each salesperson can connect their own Google account in Settings. Connecting creates a calendar named TopCoat in their Google account: appointments booked in TopCoat show up there, and events they add to that TopCoat calendar show up in the Appointments page within about 15 minutes. Personal calendars are never read or changed. Reminder timing and message wording live in the same Settings tab.
howto: Open Settings and click the Appointments tab.
Click Connect Google next to a salesperson and finish the Google sign-in in the new tab.
Come back and click Refresh to see the connected account.

title: Address autocomplete on leads and appointments
summary: The address boxes on the New Lead form and the appointment form now suggest real addresses as you type. Picking a suggestion fills in the street, city, state, and zip for you, and everything stays editable by hand. If you are offline the box works like a normal text field.
howto: Start typing a street address in the New Lead form or an appointment.
Pick the right suggestion from the list.
Fix up any field by hand if needed.

title: New Email Log: see every email the system has sent
summary: There is a new Email Log page under Sales, next to Messages. It lists every email sent from the system, newest first, with who it went to, what kind of email it was, and its delivery status (delivered, opened, clicked, or bounced). Search by customer name or email address, or filter by type, status, and date. Click any row to read the exact email that went out. Emails sent before today did not have their body saved, so those rows say so; everything from now on is captured in full. The same email history also appears at the bottom of each customer page and job page.
howto: Open Email Log under Sales in the left menu.
Type a customer name or email in the search box, or use the type, status, and date filters.
Click any row to read the full email and its delivery detail.

title: Send one message to many people with the new blast tool
summary: The Drips page now has a Manual blast card. Compose one text and/or email (with an optional AI draft you edit), pick your audience by filtering leads and customers, and uncheck anyone you want to leave out. Anyone who opted out or never gave texting consent is removed before you ever see the count, duplicates are removed, and nothing sends until you confirm a screen that states the exact number of texts and emails going out. Texts respect the 8am to 8pm window, every one carries a Reply STOP line, and the master switch gates blasts just like drips. Progress shows live on the Drips page and you can cancel the unsent remainder at any time.
howto: Open Drips (under Sales) and click New blast, then write the message or use Draft with AI and edit it.
Filter the audience, uncheck anyone to exclude, and review how many were removed for consent.
Confirm the exact counts on the last step. Watch progress on the Drips page; Cancel rest stops whatever has not sent yet.

title: Drip and blast results on the Metrics page
summary: The Metrics Sales section now shows how the automatic sequences and blasts are performing. Drip performance breaks down each sequence (lead follow-up, estimate follow-up, invoice reminders): how many are running now, messages sent, replies, and conversions, plus a chart of why sequences ended. Blast performance lists each recent blast with sent, failed, skipped, and opt-out counts and a weekly volume chart. Everything follows the same time window as the rest of Metrics and you can click through to the records behind the numbers.
howto: Open Metrics and scroll to the Sales section: the two new cards sit under Outbound touches.
Click the drip table or a blast row to see the individual sends behind the numbers.
Use the window selector at the top to change the period, same as every other card.

title: Automatic estimate follow-ups and invoice payment reminders
summary: Two new automatic sequences join the lead drip. When an estimate goes out, the customer gets warm AI-written nudges to review and sign it (days 1, 3, 7, and 14), each carrying their real signing link, and the sequence stops itself the instant they sign, decline, reply, or ask for a change. When an invoice first goes out, the job starts polite payment reminders (right away, then +3, +7, +14 days) that always show the real remaining balance and pay link; a partial payment keeps them coming with the lower balance, and the payment that clears it stops them immediately. Both ship in dry run under the same master switch, so nothing sends until you review the drafted copy and turn them on. Once a campaign is live and the switch is on, these send automatically, so read a few days of invoice drafts before flipping that one.
howto: Open Drips (under Sales) to see the two new campaigns and their drafted messages piling up in dry run.
Send a test estimate or invoice and watch the drafts appear; check the wording, the link, and the balance.
When you trust the copy, set a campaign to Go live. Keep the invoice campaign in dry run until you have read several days of its drafts, since those messages are about money.

title: Automatic follow-up drips for leads
summary: New leads now enroll in a 30-day follow-up sequence of up to 8 texts and emails, each one written by the AI for that specific lead. The drip stops itself the moment the lead replies, moves forward in the pipeline, is marked lost, texts STOP, or hits the touch limit, and texts only go out between 8am and 8pm. Nothing sends yet: the master switch ships OFF and the campaign starts in dry run, which drafts every message for your review on the lead page and the new Drips screen so you can see exactly what the AI would say before turning it on.
howto: Open Drips (under Sales) to see the campaign, its steps, and the drafted messages piling up in dry run.
Read a few days of drafts on the Drips screen or any lead's Activity timeline. When you like the copy, set the campaign to Go live and turn the master switch ON.
On any lead's page, use the Drip card to stop or enroll that lead by hand. A reply or a STOP always halts it automatically.

title: See how many times each lead has been contacted
summary: Every lead card on the Leads board now shows a Contacted count next to the speed-to-lead timer, pulled automatically from your outbound calls, texts, and emails in Quo and the dashboard. A lead nobody has reached out to reads Not contacted, and turns red once a new lead has been waiting over an hour. Open the lead for the full breakdown (calls, texts, emails, and when the last touch went out). There is nothing to log by hand: work the lead and the count keeps itself.
howto: Open Leads and look at any card: the Contacted count sits in the bottom corner next to the waiting timer.
Click a lead to open it; the Outreach line under the contact info shows the breakdown and the last touch.
Scan for red Not contacted labels to catch new leads that are aging with zero outreach.

title: Hot, Warm, and Cold lead scores you can sort by
summary: The AI score on each lead now reads as a labeled badge (Hot 70 and up, Warm 40 to 69, Cold under 40) on the board card and at the top of the lead page, with the AI's one-line reason under the name. A new Sort control on the board puts the hottest leads at the top of every column so you can work the best leads first. Scoring itself is unchanged: it runs when a lead arrives and when you click Refresh analysis.
howto: Open Leads: each scored card shows its Hot, Warm, or Cold badge next to the source.
Use the Sort dropdown in the filter bar and pick AI score: hot first.
Click a lead to see the score and the AI's reason right under the name, with the full game plan in the AI read panel.

title: Better looking, more useful Metrics graphs
summary: The Metrics tab traded its flat bars for real charts. Speed to lead and price per sqft now draw as trend lines with a soft gradient so you can see the direction, not just this week's number. Conversion by source gets a rate chart above its tables, and the Sales volume, Revenue collected, and Jobs completed cards carry small trend sparklines. A new Outbound touches card shows how many touches it takes to win a lead and how many open leads have never been contacted. Every number still clicks through to the records behind it, and no metric changed how it is calculated.
howto: Open Metrics and pick your time window and salesperson as usual.
Scroll to the Sales section for the new trend charts and the Outbound touches card.
Click any card, chart point, or row to see the underlying records, same as before.

title: Square footage and price per sqft on custom estimates
summary: A custom estimate can now carry its square footage. Type the sqft next to the price in the estimator's Custom card and a live price per sqft shows right there. When the customer accepts, the number rides to the job, so the job header chip, the Job Costing $ / sqft readout, and the printed work order all show it instead of "no sqft on file". The sqft is optional and never changes the price: you still type the price yourself.
howto: In the estimator, switch the estimate to Custom and type the price as usual.
Type the square footage in the new Square footage field; the $ / sqft line updates live.
Save and send as usual. After the customer accepts, the job's $ / sqft readouts and the work order pick the number up automatically. You can still adjust it later in the Sqft field on the job header.

title: Crew notes: cliff notes and watch-outs on the work order
summary: Every estimate now has a Crew notes (internal) box: a short brief for the install crew with cliff notes on what the job is and watch-outs like access, prep, and site conditions. Type it yourself or click Generate from proposal to have AI draft it from the proposal and site facts (you can edit or undo the draft, and it never invents anything not in the estimate). The notes ride to the job when the customer accepts, stay editable on the job page, and print in their own Crew Notes section on the work order. The customer never sees them: they stay off the proposal, the estimate page, and the PDF.
howto: In the estimator, scroll to the Crew notes (internal) card. Type notes, or click Generate from proposal for an AI draft you can edit or undo.
Save the estimate. When it is accepted, the notes carry to the job automatically.
Tweak them any time in the Crew notes box on the job page (Job Card section), then open View Work Order: the notes print in their own section above Issues / Notes.

title: Send all pending change orders for approval at once
summary: When a job has two or more unsigned change orders, the Change Orders card now bundles them into one approval request: one link, one page, one signature that approves them all. The customer sees each change order with its own price plus a grand total, and anything they already signed shows greyed out for context. The link stays live, so a change order added after you send it appears on the same page automatically. With just one pending change order, nothing changes: you get the same per-change-order link and buttons as before.
howto: Open a job's invoice (or the Estimate section on the job) that has two or more pending change orders. The card shows them together in one Change Orders awaiting approval box.
Use Copy batch link, Email batch, or Text batch to send the single approval link, or View to preview the page the customer sees.
When the customer signs once, every pending change order on the page flips to Signed, and the signed page doubles as the printable record.

title: Clearer product cost: per gallon or per kit
summary: Product cost in Settings is no longer ambiguous. The product editor now has two clearly labeled cost fields, cost per gallon (or box or pack) and cost per kit, and typing either one fills in the other automatically using the kit size. Job costing always uses the per-kit number, exactly as before, and every screen that shows a material cost now says which basis it is. No existing cost values changed.
howto: Open Price & Material Catalog from the left menu, go to the Products tab, and click any product to edit it.
Enter whichever number you have: the per gallon, box, or pack price off an invoice, or the per kit price. The other field fills in live from the kit size.
Save as usual. The per kit number is what gets stored and what job costing uses.

title: Split a job across two crews on the Next Day Schedule
summary: A big job can now be worked by two crews at the same time. On the Next Day Schedule, split a job to a second existing crew and it shows up under both crew columns in the same time slot, each card marked with a 2 teams badge. The printed run sheet lists the job under both crews too. Revenue, job counts, and job status all stay correct: it is still one job on one day, just with two teams on site.
howto: Open the Next Day Schedule and find the job's card in its crew column.
Click Split to 2nd crew on the card and pick the other team; a matching card appears in that crew's column.
To undo it later, click Remove 2nd team on the second card; the original crew's card stays put.

title: Your own private To-dos list
summary: There is a new To-dos item in the left menu (under Overview). It is a simple personal checklist: type an item, check it off when done, delete it when you no longer need it. Every person gets their own list, and it is completely private: nobody else can see it, not even admins. Because it is saved to your account, the same list shows up on any device you sign in from.
howto: Hover Overview in the left menu and click To-dos.
Type in the box at the top and hit Add (or press Enter) to create an item.
Check the box to mark an item done (it moves to the Completed section below), or hit the x to delete it.

title: Bell notifications now click through to what they are about
summary: Notifications in the bell menu are now clickable links, not just text. Job costing notifications (submitted for review, sent back) open that exact job's costing page, payment edited or deleted notifications open the invoice, and customer portal notifications open the job card. If a notification has nowhere sensible to go (like a deleted customer), it stays plain text. Costing links only appear for people with Job Costing access.
howto: Open the bell in the top bar and click any notification; it marks itself read and takes you to the job, invoice, or costing page it is about.
If a costing was sent back to you, clicking that notification lands you right on that job's costing view with the reason banner.
Notifications without a pointer cursor are informational only and have no page to open.

title: Invoicing: last-sent dates fixed, plus a Communication history on every invoice
summary: The last-sent column on the Invoicing list now shows the real date of the newest invoice email or text for each completed job (a bug made it always show never sent or a dash, even after a send). Every invoice page also has a new Communication history section listing each invoice email and text for that job: when it went out (Phoenix time), who it went to, the subject, its delivery status, and which staff member sent it. Failed attempts show too, in red, so nothing hides.
howto: Open Invoicing and check the completed section: jobs you have invoiced now show the actual last-sent date instead of never sent.
Click View Invoice on any job and scroll to Communication history to see every invoice email and text with its time, recipient, and status.
Statuses update on their own as emails deliver: sent means it left, delivered means it reached the inbox, and failed or bounced means it did not.

title: Simpler Price & Material Catalog
summary: The catalog is easier to read and manage. Each flake color now carries its own default basecoat right on the product (the separate Color Pairings tab is gone), and every flake requires one so estimates always auto-fill the right basecoat. System Types now shows a compact one-line summary per system (name, active, and the pricing percentages); click a system to see its full recipe. The old Requires flake and Requires basecoat switches are gone too: a system's recipe slots now decide which color pickers appear.
howto: To set a flake's basecoat, open the Catalog, click the flake under Flake Materials, and pick its Default basecoat in the product window.
On the System Types tab, click any system's row to expand its recipe slots; click again to collapse it.
Nothing changes for reps: picking a flake on an estimate still fills in its basecoat automatically.

title: Estimator: the proposal now builds live as you estimate
summary: Standard estimates now show the customer-facing proposal right in the estimator, in a new Proposal / Scope of work panel. It fills in from your scope templates the moment an area has a system and square footage, the AI writes the polished version by itself on the first save (once the scope questions are answered), and after that it only rewrites when you tap Regenerate proposal, so your edits are never lost. You can edit the text right in the panel before saving or sending.
howto: Build a standard estimate as usual; the proposal drafts itself in the new panel as you go.
Answer the Finish the scope questions and save; the AI writes the polished proposal automatically the first time.
Edit the text in the panel any time, or tap Regenerate proposal after a change; it always asks before replacing text you edited.

title: Estimator: custom estimate mode for one-off jobs
summary: The estimator now has a Standard/Custom switch at the top. Custom is for one-off work that does not fit the material calculator: you type the scope of work and the price yourself, and add-ons still work. An optional Polish with AI button cleans up your typed scope (it never changes your meaning, exclusions, or dollar figures, and you can undo it).
howto: Open the estimator and tap Custom at the top (next to the customer card).
Type the scope of work and the price, then save; the proposal and PDF show exactly what you typed.
Optional: tap Polish with AI to clean up the wording, and Undo polish if you liked yours better.

title: New material category: Polycoat
summary: The Price and Material Catalog now has a Polycoat category for the new waterproof deck system's materials. Polycoat products get their own section in the catalog, and a system's recipe slots can pull Polycoat products, so the Polycoat system can be wired up end to end. Pricing works like the other liquid categories (per gallon).
howto: Open the Price and Material Catalog and click + Add product.
Pick Polycoat as the Material type and save; it appears under the new Polycoat section.
To use it in a system, edit the system's recipe slot and choose Polycoat as the material type.

title: Estimator: separate name, company, and address fields
summary: The estimator's customer card now starts with a Residential or Commercial choice. Residential asks for a first and last name; Commercial asks for the company name (required) plus an optional contact person. The address is now real fields (Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip), and once a Google key is configured, typing in Address 1 suggests real addresses and fills the city, state, and zip for you. Everything stays editable by hand, and the estimator still works fully offline. Commercial estimates show the company name on the customer's proposal page and carry it onto the customer record when they accept.
howto: Open the estimator and pick Residential or Commercial at the top of the Customer card.
For a business, type the company name; add a contact person if you have one.
Start typing the street in Address 1 and pick a suggestion to fill city, state, and zip, or just type them in.

title: Approve each crew member's bonus when you finalize
summary: Finalizing a job costing now opens an approval step. It lists each crew member with the suggested bonus already filled in, and you can change any amount before it is recorded. The crew pool total updates live as you edit, and it is simply the sum of what you approve (there is no re-split). What gets recorded keeps a full trail: the originally suggested amount, the approved amount, and who approved it. The suggested pool also shows next to each job in the Submitted for review list, so you can see it before opening the job.
howto: On a submitted job, click Finalize Job Costing to open the approval step.
Adjust any crew member's amount; watch the crew pool total update.
Click Approve and Finalize; the Bonus Report pending payout shows the approved numbers.

title: Send a job costing back with a reason
summary: When you send a submitted job costing back to the person who submitted it, you now type a short reason for why. The reason is required. The submitter sees it three ways: a banner right on the job, a bell notification, and a message in the #epoxysales Slack channel. Every reason is kept as a history on the job, so if it goes back and forth you can read the whole thread.
howto: On a submitted job costing, click Send back and type what needs fixing.
The submitter gets a banner on the job, a bell, and a Slack note.
Open Send-back history on the job to read every reason with who and when.

title: The Pending Jobs panel now fits the calendar
summary: On the Job Schedule, the Pending Jobs panel used to have a fixed height that cut a short calendar off or ran long on a tall one. Now it sizes to the calendar beside it: when there are only a few pending jobs the panel stays short, and when there are many the panel matches the calendar's height and the list scrolls inside itself, so the page no longer grows a second scrollbar. Switching between Week and 3 weeks adjusts it automatically.
howto: Open the Job Schedule; the Pending Jobs panel lines up with the calendar height.
With many pending jobs, scroll inside the panel to see them all.
Toggle Week and 3 weeks; the panel resizes to match.

title: Click a pending job to see its details
summary: On the Job Schedule, the cards under Pending Jobs are now clickable. Click one (anywhere on the card) to open a quick, read-only look at the job: customer and address, proposal number and revenue, the system with its color, total square footage and estimated hours, the scope or notes, plus the sales team, status, and any reschedule owed. It is view-only, so nothing can be changed by accident. The + Schedule button on the card opens the scheduler as before, and the small x still removes the job from the list.
howto: On the Job Schedule, click a card under Pending Jobs to open its details.
Read the job over; nothing here changes the job.
Use + Schedule from the card (or inside the details) when you are ready to schedule it.

title: Jobs now carry their system, and the calendar colors them automatically
summary: When a customer accepts an estimate, the job now keeps the system (or systems) from that estimate, so it shows its color on the Job Schedule and can pull materials and per-system numbers right away, with no re-typing. Jobs that came straight from DripJobs never had a system, so scheduling one now asks you to pick a system before you can save. The + Add Job form asks the same way. This is the fix for the schedule system dropdown that used to open blank.
howto: Schedule a job as usual; if it has no system yet, pick one in the System type box before saving.
In + Add Job, choose a System type (it creates the job's first area for you).
Estimator jobs already carry their system, so their color shows on the calendar on their own.

title: The schedule day picker opens on this month
summary: When you open a scheduled job to change its days, the calendar now opens on the current month instead of the job's first scheduled day. For a job that spans two months (say late June into July) that means you land where you are actually working. If the job has days in another month, a line at the top of the picker names them and jumps you there in one tap, so nothing looks lost.
howto: Open a scheduled job; the day picker starts on this month.
If a line at the top says days are in another month, tap it to jump to them.
Use the arrows to move between months as before.

title: Click a week's revenue to see how it adds up
summary: The revenue shown next to each week on the Job Schedule is prorated: a job's price is split evenly across its scheduled days, so a job that runs into two weeks shows part of its price in each. Click the week revenue (or tap it on a phone) to open a breakdown that lists each job, its contract price, how many of its days fall in that week, and the slice that adds to the total. Touch-up callbacks are listed as left out, since they are no charge. It is scheduled contract revenue, not cash collected and not profit.
howto: On the Job Schedule 3-week view, click a week's revenue number.
Read each job's contract, its days this week over its total days, and the slice.
Press Escape or click away to close it.

title: New left menu: fewer items, grouped into flyouts
summary: The left menu was a long list of every screen. It is now six groups (Overview, Sales, Production, Finance, Admin, and Help). Click a group and a small submenu opens with the screens inside it. Nothing was removed, just tidied: Bonus Report and Commission now live under Finance (in a Reports section), DripJobs Sync Health lives under Admin (in a Diagnostics section), Price & Material Catalog is now called Pricing, and Next Day Schedule is now called Next Day. On a phone, tap the Menu button to open the groups. Every old bookmark and link still works.
howto: Click a group like Sales or Finance to open its submenu, then pick a screen.
Find Bonus Report and Commission under Finance; find Sync Health under Admin.
On a phone, tap Menu, then tap a group to expand it.

title: Messages now shows calls and texts together
summary: The Messages tab is one inbox that merges texts and call logs into a single conversation per phone number, newest first. Use the All, Texts, and Calls chips to filter. Every conversation is clickable, even a number that is not yet a customer: open it to see the full back-and-forth and reply right there. On an unknown number you can Attach to customer (which files all of that number's texts and calls under the customer you pick) or Create lead (which starts a new lead with the phone already filled in).
howto: Open Messages and use All, Texts, or Calls to filter the list.
Click any conversation to see its full history and send a reply.
On an unknown number, click Attach to customer or Create lead.

title: Cleaner Job Schedule toolbar
summary: The Job Schedule toolbar is reorganized so the controls sit together and read left to right: the Today and back/forward arrows with the date range on the left, the Week and 3 weeks buttons right next to them, and a single + Add button on the far right. The + Add button opens a short menu with Add Job, Add Task, Holiday, and Day Off, so the four buttons that used to be spread across the bar are now in one place.
howto: Use the arrows or Today to move the date range, then Week or 3 weeks to change the span.
Click + Add on the right for Add Job, Add Task, Holiday, or Day Off.
Click away or press Escape to close the Add menu.

title: Next Day and Job Schedule now fit your phone
summary: On a phone, the Next Day Schedule and the Job Schedule no longer make you scroll sideways. Next Day stacks each crew with a heading that sticks as you scroll, shows full-width job cards, and floats any not-yet-scheduled work to the top so it is the first thing you see. The Job Schedule turns the seven-column calendar into a simple top-to-bottom list of days, with Pending Jobs in a section you can tap to open or collapse. On a computer both screens look exactly as before.
howto: Open Next Day Schedule or Job Schedule on your phone; no more sideways scrolling.
On Next Day, jobs with no slot yet sit at the top of the list.
On the Job Schedule, tap the Pending Jobs header to open or collapse it.

title: Archive an estimate (and restore it)
summary: An estimate you no longer want can be archived from its page: it leaves the list and its customer link stops working. Archiving is a soft delete, so nothing is really gone. Open the Archived filter on the Estimates list to see archived ones and restore any of them. Archiving an accepted estimate does NOT touch the job it created; the job stays on the Jobs page and the schedule.
howto: Open an estimate and click Archive. Confirm the prompt (it warns if a job already exists).
To bring one back, open Estimates, click Archived, and hit Restore on the row.
A restored estimate comes back whole, with its areas, line items, and scope.

title: Moisture vapor barrier is now per area
summary: The moisture vapor barrier used to be one switch for the whole estimate, which was wrong when only one area needs it. Now each area has its own MVB checkbox, defaulted off. Check it on the garage and leave it off the patio, and only the garage carries the barrier's cost and gets the moisture-barrier scope language. An MVB-only job is just an area on the new MVB Only system.
howto: In the estimator, tick Add moisture vapor barrier on each area that needs one.
The price and the scope update for just those areas.
For an MVB-only job with no coating, pick the MVB Only system on the area.

title: See how the price was reached, and adjust it
summary: The estimator now shows the work behind the number: the price per square foot up top, the full cost stack (materials, labor and hours, sundries, add-ons, commission, gross profit), and a plain-English line explaining how the price was calculated, including when charm-pricing nudged it under a round number. You can override the total sell price by typing a new number; the gross profit updates live and turns red below target. A reason is required to save a changed price, and going below the gross-profit floor asks you to confirm.
howto: Look under the price for $/sqft, the cost breakdown, and the one-line explanation.
To change the price, type a new Sell price; the gross profit updates as you type.
Enter a reason for the change (required), and confirm if it drops below the floor.

title: Estimates now include a 2% sundries and disposables cost
summary: Every estimate now bakes in a 2% sundries and disposables cost (tape, blades, plastic, mixing sticks, grinder consumables) on top of materials, labor, and commission, so the price covers the small stuff that used to be invisible. This changes every price by roughly 2% of its cost. The rate is adjustable in Price & Material Catalog. The customer still sees one total price, exactly as before.
howto: Nothing to do; new estimates include it automatically.
To change the rate, edit the sundries percent in Price & Material Catalog.
It shows as its own line in the internal cost breakdown; the customer never sees it.

title: Price per square foot on jobs
summary: Jobs now show price per square foot so an outlier is easy to spot. The Jobs list has a sortable $/sqft column, the job costing panel shows $/sqft next to revenue with the square footage and system behind it, and Metrics breaks $/sqft down by system (average and median) and over time. A job with no square footage on file shows a dash and is left out of the averages, with the count of excluded jobs shown.
howto: On the Jobs tab, click the $/sqft column header to sort by it.
Open a job's costing to see its $/sqft with the sqft and system it is based on.
In Metrics, check the by-system average and median and the monthly trend.

title: Preview an estimate before you send it
summary: The estimate page has a Preview button that shows the exact page the customer will get, including the scope, the line items, and the optional add-ons, without sending anything. It opens in a window over the dashboard, the accept and decline buttons are shown disabled, and a PREVIEW banner runs across the top so there is no confusing it with the real thing. Nothing is sent and the customer link stays private.
howto: Open an estimate and click Preview.
Look it over the way the customer will see it. Close the window when you are done.
When it looks right, use Send to customer to actually send it.

title: The estimator asks about blanks in the scope
summary: Some of the scope templates have blanks in them (for example the area a coating is going on, or the project duration). The estimator now asks you to fill those in while you are on site, in a Finish the scope section, and the answers drop straight into the customer's scope of work. If you saved quickly and skipped them, the estimate page shows the same questions so you can finish at the desk. If a blank is still there when you go to send, you get a clear warning first, because a customer should never read the word BLANK in a document they are signing.
howto: In the estimator, fill in anything under Finish the scope before you save.
On the estimate page, use the Finish the scope card to answer anything left, then the scope rewrites itself.
If you try to send with a blank still in the scope, confirm the warning only if you really mean to.

title: A heads-up before you start a second estimate on a lead
summary: If a lead already has an open estimate, Start estimate now asks before creating another one, so a lead does not quietly end up with three. It lists the open estimates with their number, status, and price; you can open one of those, or create a new one anyway if that is what you meant to do. Estimates that were declined or lost do not trigger the warning, since re-estimating after a no is normal.
howto: Click Start estimate on a lead as usual.
If it already has an open estimate, pick Open to jump to it, or Create new anyway to keep going.
The lead's Estimates section shows the count so you can see it before you click.

title: One estimate can cover a garage, a patio, and more, each its own system
summary: Every area on an estimate now picks its own system, so a flake garage plus a quartz patio is a single estimate and a single price. Each area is priced with its own recipe, and the gross profit target is the square-foot-weighted average of the systems in play, so a small high-margin area does not drag the whole number. The comps panel keys off the biggest system and tells you when the estimate spans more than one.
howto: In the estimator, each area row has its own System dropdown next to its square footage. Change it per area.
Add as many areas as the job has; the price, gross profit, and hours roll up from all of them.
When an estimate spans systems, the Comparable jobs panel says which system the comps cover.

title: Add-ons come from a catalog and carry a real cost
summary: An Add-ons section in the estimator lets you drop in stem walls, joint filling, upgrades, or drive time from a catalog, with the price and cost prefilled and still editable. Because every add-on carries a cost, gross profit stays honest even when you pile on upsells. Optional add-ons stay out of the total until the customer picks them, and you can see both the base price and the price if they take everything. A free-typed one-off line is still there for whatever the catalog does not have.
howto: In the estimator's Add-ons section, pick from the catalog or click One-off line to type your own.
Set the price and cost; tick Optional for anything the customer chooses on their end.
The price box shows the base total and, when there are optional items, the total if every one is taken.
Manage the catalog in Price & Material Catalog under the new Add-ons tab: set each one's price, cost, unit, and the scope paragraph it adds to the customer's scope of work.

title: Estimates write their own scope of work
summary: Every estimate now assembles a customer-facing scope of work from your real templates, filling in the square footage, the areas, and whether stem walls and past-the-garage are included from the estimate itself. It never rewrites your exclusions or cure-time language, only substitutes the job's details. It writes itself on save, and you can Edit the text by hand: once you do, it is never overwritten without your explicit Regenerate click, and if the estimate changes afterward it tells you the scope is out of date.
howto: Save an estimate and the Scope of work card fills in automatically (needs a connection; offline saves generate once you reconnect).
Click Edit text to adjust wording by hand. After that, the AI never replaces your words unless you click Regenerate and confirm.
If you change the estimate after editing the scope, a note tells you it is out of date so you can Regenerate when ready.

title: Estimator prices with just the system and square footage
summary: You no longer have to pick a basecoat or flake color to get a price. Every system's recipe now carries default products, and an unpicked flake is priced at the standard flake cost with the color left TBD for the customer to choose after the presentation. Flake job pricing now matches the price sheet: a 1000 sqft garage quotes about $5,345 at the new 52% gross profit target, and the target is editable per system in the catalog.
howto: Open the estimator, pick the system, type the square footage, and the price appears. Nothing else is required.
Leave the flake color unpicked if the customer has not chosen; the price already includes standard flake and the color stays editable on the estimate page.
To tune margins, open Price & Material Catalog, edit a system type, and set its Target GP %. Blank means the global default.

title: Customers can now sign an estimate online
summary: Send to customer on an estimate's page emails them a private link where they can review the scope and line items, tick optional add-ons (the total updates as they choose), and accept and sign by typing their name. They can also request changes with a message or decline with a reason. Accepting creates the job automatically on both the Jobs page and the Job Schedule, with the areas and work-order details carried over. The link stays private (it does not work at all) until you send it.
howto: Open an estimate and click Send to customer. Review the prefilled email and send it.
The customer opens their link, ticks any optional items, and signs by typing their name. You get a Slack and email notification either way.
On accept, the job appears on the Jobs page and in the Job Schedule's pending list automatically, and the lead moves to Accepted.
If they request changes, edit the estimate and click Re-send: same number, same link, new sent date.

title: Estimator opens over the dashboard and asks for way less
summary: Start estimate now opens the estimator in a window over the dashboard instead of a new tab. System, square footage, and an MVB switch are all it needs for a price; products, colors, and the work order live in a collapsed More detail section. A sell price or discount box shows the margin live, and comps from your own completed jobs plus an AI price read sit next to the number.
howto: Open a lead and click Start estimate, or use the Estimator button in the sidebar for a walk-up.
Pick the system and type the square footage. The price, comps, and AI read appear on the right.
Type a sell price or a discount percent to see the gross profit move; it turns red below the system's target.
Save. The window closes and the estimate's own page opens.

title: Estimates are now real numbered records with their own pages
summary: Every saved estimate gets a sequential number (EST-102026 and up) and its own page: customer info, price and margin, line items with optional add-ons the customer can take, flake color you can fill in after the presentation, and the comps and AI read that priced it. A new Estimates section in the sidebar lists them all with search.
howto: Click Estimates in the sidebar to see the list, newest first. Search by number, customer, phone, or address.
Click any row to open the estimate's page. Edit reopens the estimator with everything filled in.
Use + Add optional item for upsells like stem walls or an extra bay; they stay out of the total until ticked.
Mark accepted or Mark lost records the outcome. Sending it to the customer arrives in the next update.

title: Start estimate now carries the lead with it
summary: Hitting Start estimate on a lead opens the estimator already tied to that lead, so the estimate shows up on the lead's page and counts in the lead's value instead of floating loose.
howto: Open a lead from the Leads board and click Start estimate.
Look for the Lead chip next to the PEC Estimator title, it names the lead the estimate will attach to.
Build and save as usual. An estimate saved offline still attaches once the phone gets signal.

title: Click a lead for its full story plus an AI game plan
summary: Clicking a card on the Leads board opens the lead's page: contact info, notes, and the full activity timeline on the left; an AI read on the right with a score, the single best next step, call talking points, and ready-to-copy text and email drafts. Nothing sends itself; you copy, you send.
howto: Click any card on the Leads board. Back returns to the board.
The AI panel leads with the next action; Copy buttons grab the text or email draft (the text copy stays locked unless the lead agreed to texts).
Change the stage right from the page, edit notes, or hit Refresh analysis after a call.
Start estimate opens the estimator with the lead attached. Once OpenPhone is connected, calls and transcripts appear in the timeline on their own.

title: Metrics: new Sales section shows which ad money works
summary: The Metrics tab has a new Sales section: price per square foot by month with a per-system breakdown, speed to lead (how fast new leads get a first contact), conversion by source and campaign, and the open lead pipeline with an AI-written weekly read.
howto: Open Metrics and scroll to the Sales section; the window picker at the top applies to it too.
Conversion by source and campaign shows leads, accepted count, rate, and sold value per ad source.
Speed to lead is the median time from a lead arriving to first contact; keep it under an hour.
Click Refresh on the AI weekly read for a fresh 3-4 sentence take on the funnel.

title: $/sqft on jobs, with a Sqft field you can backfill
summary: Jobs now show their price per square foot on the job page header and on Jobs pipeline cards. A new Sqft field on the job page lets you fill in square footage for older jobs; a value you type there always wins over the estimate areas.
howto: Open a job; the header shows a $/sqft chip when the square footage is known.
To backfill an older job, type the square footage into the new Sqft field next to Price and save.
Jobs pipeline cards show $/sqft under the price when it is known.

title: New Leads board: work every lead from first click to sold
summary: A new Leads tab (next to Messages) shows every lead as a card in six columns, from New to Accepted or Lost. Drag cards between columns as you work them. New leads show how long they have been waiting, turning red after an hour, so nobody sits unclaimed.
howto: Open the Leads tab. Each column shows its count and total estimate value; the top shows open leads and open pipeline value.
Drag a card to the next column as you work the lead. Dropping on Lost asks for a quick reason.
Use the filters for source, campaign, owner, dates, or search by name, phone, or email.
Walk-ins and phone leads: click + New Lead and type them in.

title: New leads flow straight into HQ (no more DripJobs for new leads)
summary: Facebook and Google leads now land in HQ automatically the moment someone submits a form, each with an instant AI read: a summary, a 1-100 score, and a suggested next step. Duplicate submissions fold into the existing lead instead of cluttering the list.
howto: Nothing to do day to day; leads arrive on their own once the Zaps are connected.
A second inquiry from the same person attaches to their existing lead as a note instead of creating a copy.
The Leads board to work them lands next; the data is already collecting.

title: Archived jobs no longer sit in Invoicing
summary: Archiving a job now removes it from every Invoicing section and the AR totals, the same way voiding does. Cancelled jobs stop inflating pending deposits, and their public pay links go dead so nobody can pay a cancelled job.
howto: Archive a cancelled job from its job page like before; it disappears from Invoicing on its own.
The Total AR number and the section totals no longer count archived jobs.
The job itself is untouched; it is just out of the money views.

title: Day numbers now always follow the calendar
summary: Day 1 is always the earliest scheduled day. Before, the schedule window numbered days in the order you clicked them, so adding an earlier day could leave the numbers out of order. Existing jobs were renumbered too.
howto: Open a job's schedule and add a day before the current start; the new day becomes Day 1 automatically.
The little corner numbers in the day picker and the Day column on the job page both follow date order now.
Nothing to do for old jobs; they were renumbered in the same update.

title: Short notes on the schedule, like "flake portion"
summary: Each stretch of scheduled days can now carry a short note that shows right on the calendar bar, on the week run sheet, and in the bar's hover text. Perfect for splitting one job into its flake days and patio days at a glance.
howto: Open a job from the calendar. Below the day picker you'll see one note box per stretch of back-to-back days, labeled with its dates.
Type a short label (up to 60 characters), like flake portion, and Save.
The note shows on the calendar bar in both views and in the job's schedule table. Hover the bar to read it in full.

title: Pull install days off the calendar for rescheduling
summary: When a job (or just part of one) gets bumped, open it from the Job Schedule and click Reschedule. The pulled days come off the calendar and the job shows in the Pending column with an amber Reschedule badge until you rebook it. Crew, hours, and price stay on the job.
howto: Click the job's bar on the calendar to open the schedule window.
Deselect the day or days getting pulled (deselect all of them to pull the whole job), then click Reschedule.
The job shows in Pending on the left with an amber badge like Reschedule, 2 days, plus the date it was pulled from.
When you rebook it, click + Schedule on the card, pick the new days, and Save. The badge clears on its own.

title: The job page got a clean new layout
summary: The estimate is now a Line Items table with the totals at a glance, each change order sits in its own orange box with its status, and the whole page is tidier: notes and job card fields side by side, and a Save bar that follows you as you scroll.
howto: Open any job. The estimate shows as a Line Items table; click a line name to open and edit that line, then click Done.
Each change order has its own box with a Pending signature or Signed pill and its send buttons.
The Totals section at the bottom of the estimate shows Subtotal, Change orders, and the grand Total in the dark bar.
Save job now rides in a bar at the bottom of the screen, so you never scroll to find it.

title: Estimate total, Add change order, and Download PDF moved to the top of the job
summary: The estimate total now shows in the button row at the top of every job, next to Add change order and Download PDF. No more scrolling to the Estimate section to see the price or grab the estimate PDF.
howto: Open any job. The top row now ends with the estimate total, Add change order, and Download PDF.
The total updates live as you type line prices, same as before.
Add change order and Download PDF work exactly like they did in the Estimate section.

title: Job page buttons are bolder and grouped on the left
summary: The action buttons at the top of a job (Back to jobs, View Invoice, Copy portal link, View customer portal, Messages & Calls) now sit together on the left and stand out more, so they are easier to spot at a glance.
howto: Open any job. All five action buttons now sit together at the top left.
Messages & Calls is the last button in that row and still turns orange while you are on the conversation view.
Every button does exactly what it did before; only the look and placement changed.

title: The customer invoice page got a professional new look
summary: The invoice customers open from their pay link now looks like a premium brand: a bold dark header with the amount due front and center, clean line items, and clearer payment buttons. Same links, same payment options.
howto: Nothing to do. Every existing /pay invoice link wears the new design automatically.
Email or text an invoice as usual; the customer's link opens the new page.
All payment behavior is unchanged: card, bank transfer, deposit, check, cash, and Zelle work exactly as before.

title: Messages & Calls got a phone-app look and moved into the job's top toolbar
summary: The job's Messages & Calls feed now looks like a real texting app: chat bubbles with names and avatars, call summaries in a card, and a cleaner compose box. The button to open it now sits in the toolbar at the top of the job.
howto: Open a job and click Messages & Calls in the toolbar at the top. Click it again to go back to the job details.
Calls show their AI summary as bullet points; click View transcript on a call to read the whole conversation.
Type in the box at the bottom to text the customer. Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line.
The Texts and Calls cards on the customer profile use the same new look.

title: TopCoat now tells you what changed
summary: New features show up in this popup when you sign in, and the full history lives in Help.
howto: When something new ships, you will see this popup once at sign in. Click Got it and you will not see those items again.
To browse everything later, open the Help tab. The What's New card at the top lists every update.
You can also ask the help assistant (the ? bubble, bottom right) how any new feature works.

title: Pending bank transfers show on the customer invoice
summary: While a customer's bank transfer is clearing (3 to 5 days), their invoice shows it as PENDING, the amount due drops, and the pay buttons hide so nobody pays twice.
howto: Nothing to do. The customer's /pay page handles it automatically the moment they pay by bank.
In Invoicing, the completed list shows an ACH pending chip under the balance so you know not to chase that customer.
If you try to email or text an invoice that has a pending transfer, TopCoat asks you to confirm first.

title: Messages and Calls tab on every job
summary: Open a job and see the customer's texts and phone calls in one feed, in time order, and text them right from the job.
howto: Jobs tab, open a job, click Messages & Calls (top right, next to View customer portal).
Calls show the AI summary; click Transcript to read the whole conversation.
Type in the box at the bottom to text the customer. Replies show up when you hit Refresh.

title: Customers can pay invoices by bank transfer (ACH)
summary: The Pay online button on invoices now offers bank transfer as well as card. Bank transfers cost us about $5 instead of about 3 percent.
howto: Nothing changes when you send an invoice; the customer picks card or bank on the Stripe payment page.
Bank transfers take 3 to 5 business days to land. The payment records itself automatically when it clears.
If a transfer bounces, the job gets a red ACH failed chip in Invoicing and Dylan gets an alert.

title: Itemized subcontractor expenses on Job Costing
summary: Record who was paid what on subbed-out jobs, and flag a whole job as subcontracted so the crew bonus math skips it.
howto: Job Costing, open the job, find the Subcontractors card. Add a line with the sub's name and the dollar amount.
The total flows into the job's costs and profit automatically.
If the whole job was subbed out, tick This job is subcontracted; hours expectations and crew bonus then skip it.

title: Change orders that carry real scope
summary: Add a change order from the job page with a system and square footage; pricing suggests itself, materials flow to costing, and the customer can sign it online.
howto: Jobs tab, open the job, click Add change order in the Estimate section (also on the Invoicing detail).
Pick the system and square feet and the price pre-fills like the estimator; or use Simple mode for a title and amount.
In the Change orders card you can email or text the customer a signing link and watch the badge flip to Signed.

title: Phone calls with AI summaries on customer profiles
summary: Every call to or from the office number now logs on the customer's profile with a summary, next steps, and the full transcript.
howto: Customers tab, open a customer, scroll to the Calls card.
Each call shows who called, how long it lasted, and what it was about.
Click Transcript to read the word-for-word conversation.

title: Last invoiced column and a Cancelled jobs section
summary: Invoicing now shows when each completed job was last sent an invoice (red if never), and cancelled jobs live in their own section with a Restore button.
howto: Invoicing tab, completed section: the Last invoiced column sits right after Age. Red means send the invoice.
Jobs tab, bottom: the Cancelled / archived jobs card lists every archived job.
Click Restore on an archived job to bring it back to Jobs and the Schedule.

title: Job costing submit-for-review flow
summary: Non-admin staff submit a finished costing for review instead of finalizing it; Dylan reviews and finalizes, which records the crew bonus.
howto: Fill in the job's costing as usual, then click Submit for review. Your numbers lock while it waits.
Dylan sees it in the Submitted for review queue on the Job Costing page and finalizes or sends it back.
Team member hours are entered per person on the job page; they drive the bonus math.

title: Text customers from TopCoat
summary: Two-way texting from customer profiles through the office number, plus a Text invoice button that sends the pay link.
howto: Customers tab, open a customer, use the Texts card to send and read messages.
On an invoice, click Text invoice to send the customer their pay link by text.
Customers who reply STOP are opted out automatically and TopCoat will refuse to text them.

title: In-house estimator (beta)
summary: A TopCoat estimator that prices jobs from square footage and system type, using the same catalog and math as Job Costing.
howto: Open it from the Estimator button in the nav (admins and estimators only while in beta).
Enter the areas and square footage; the price suggestion comes from cost plus target margin.
Talk to Dylan before using it on a live customer while it is in beta.
